Additive change: the existing per-IP throttle on redirects stays exactly as it is; per-key limiting applies only to link creation and redirects are never limited by key.", "scenario": "brownfield"}, "prompt": "REQUIREMENT\nAdd per-API-key rate limiting to the existing URL shortener.\n\nKeys come from the environment, not from the database. The variable SHORTENER_API_KEYS holds a comma-separated list of key:quota pairs, so a key named alpha with a quota of 100 and a key named beta with a quota of 20 are written as two such pairs. The quota is requests per minute for link creation. There is no admin surface and no schema change; an unknown key is treated as no key.\n\nA caller presents its key in an X-API-Key header. A request carrying a known key is limited against that key's quota. A request with no key, or an unknown one, keeps the existing per-IP limit exactly as it behaves today, so existing clients continue to work unchanged.\n\nA caller over its quota receives HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header giving whole seconds until the window resets.\n\nThis change is additive. The existing per-IP throttle on redirects stays exactly as it is; do not remove or weaken it. Per-key limiting applies only to link creation, and redirects are never limited by key.\n\nA previous attempt at this stage was rejected by the quality gate. Fix the cause rather than working around the check.\nGate result: exit gate blocked by security.open_redirect (high x2)\n- [high] security.open_redirect at analyze.json:77: redirect handling never validates the destination scheme; restrict it to an http/https allowlist before issuing the Location header\n- [high] security.open_redirect at analyze.json:77: redirect handling never blocks internal hosts; localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 and the 169.254.169.254 metadata endpoint stay reachable\n\nEXISTING CODE\n--- README.md ---\n# URL Shortener\n\nPublic JSON API that turns a caller supplied public `http(s)` URL into an\nunguessable base62 short code, redirects visitors until the link expires and\nexposes per-link click analytics that contain no visitor IP addresses.\n\n## Run\n\n```bash\npip install -r requirements.txt\nuvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000\n```\n\n## Endpoints\n\n| Method | Path | Purpose |\n| ------ | ---- | ------- |\n| POST | `/api/links` | Create a short link (`{\"url\": \"...\", \"expires_at\": \"...\"}`) |\n| GET | `/api/links/{code}/stats` | Click analytics (`limit`, `offset`) |\n| GET | `/health` | Liveness; `{\"status\":\"ok\"}` or 503 `{\"status\":\"degraded\"}` |\n| GET | `/{code}` | 307 redirect to the stored destination |\n\nErrors always use `{\"error\": {\"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\"}}`.\n\n## Configuration\n\n| Variable | Default | Purpose |\n| -------- | ------- | ------- |\n| `LINKS_DB_PATH` | `./links.db` | SQLite database file |\n| `LINKS_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8000` | Origin used for `short_url` |\n| `LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_DAYS` | `30` | Default link lifetime |\n| `LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH` | `2048` | Maximum accepted URL length |\n| `LINKS_CODE_LENGTH` | `7` | Base62 code length |\n| `LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | Insert attempts on code collision |\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` | `10` | Creations per client per window |\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `60` | Rolling window length |\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | `false`/`0`/`no` disables the limiter |\n| `LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR` | `false` | Use first `X-Forwarded-For` entry |\n| `LINKS_STATS_DEFAULT_LIMIT` | `50` | Default clicks page size |\n| `LINKS_STATS_MAX_LIMIT` | `500` | Maximum clicks page size |\n| `LINKS_DNS_RESOLUTION_ENABLED` | `true` | Resolve and denylist-check hosts |\n| `LINKS_LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | Root log level |\n\nNo secrets are read or stored by the service.\n\n## Security notes\n\n* Scheme allow-list (`http`, `https`) plus an address denylist covering\n loopback, private, link-local (including `169.254.169.254`), unique-local,\n CGNAT, multicast, unspecified and reserved ranges, with IPv4-mapped,\n IPv4-compatible, 6to4, Teredo and decimal/octal/hex IPv4 literals decoded.\n* The service never performs an outbound HTTP request to a destination.\n* Redirect targets come only from the validated, stored row.\n* Rate limiting keys on a per-boot salted hash of the client address; no IP is\n written to the database, to a file or to a log.\n\n\n--- app/__init__.py ---\n\"\"\"URL shortener service package.\n\nExposes :func:`app.main.create_app`, the application factory, and the module\nlevel ``app`` ASGI application used by uvicorn.\n\"\"\"\n\n__all__ = [\"__version__\"]\n\n__version__ = \"1.0.0\"\n\n\n--- app/codes.py ---\n\"\"\"Short code generation.\n\nCodes are drawn from a cryptographically secure random source; they are never\nderived from a database row id or any other sequence.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\nimport string\n\nALPHABET = string.ascii_uppercase + string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits\n\n\ndef generate_code(length: int) -> str:\n \"\"\"Generate a base62 short code.\n\n ``length`` is the number of characters to produce. Returns a string of\n exactly ``length`` characters drawn uniformly from ``[A-Za-z0-9]`` using\n :mod:`secrets`. Raises :class:`ValueError` when ``length`` is not positive.\n \"\"\"\n if length <= 0:\n raise ValueError(\"code length must be positive\")\n return \"\".join(secrets.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(length))\n\n\n--- app/config.py ---\n\"\"\"Environment driven configuration for the URL shortener service.\n\nAll settings come from environment variables with the exact names and defaults\nfixed by the design document. No secrets are read or stored here.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport os\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom typing import Mapping, Optional\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(\"links.config\")\n\n#: Hard ceiling applied to the accepted ``url`` length regardless of\n#: ``LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH``. It bounds the string that ever reaches the\n#: database and the pydantic request model.\nABSOLUTE_MAX_URL_LENGTH = 8192\n\n#: Hard ceiling for the client supplied ``expires_at`` string.\nMAX_EXPIRES_AT_LENGTH = 64\n\n#: Hard ceiling for ``LINKS_BASE_URL``.\nMAX_BASE_URL_LENGTH = 512\n\n_FALSE_VALUES = frozenset({\"false\", \"0\", \"no\"})\n_TRUE_VALUES = frozenset({\"true\", \"1\", \"yes\"})\n\n_VALID_LOG_LEVELS = frozenset(\n {\"CRITICAL\", \"ERROR\", \"WARNING\", \"INFO\", \"DEBUG\", \"NOTSET\"}\n)\n\n\ndef _get(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str, default: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Read a raw environment value.\n\n Returns the value for ``name`` in ``env`` or ``default`` when the variable\n is missing or empty. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n raw = env.get(name)\n if raw is None:\n return default\n raw = raw.strip()\n if not raw:\n return default\n return raw\n\n\ndef _get_int(\n env: Mapping[str, str],\n name: str,\n default: str,\n minimum: int,\n maximum: int,\n) -> int:\n \"\"\"Read an integer setting, clamped to a safe range.\n\n Returns the parsed integer, or the parsed default when the environment\n value is not an integer or falls outside ``[minimum, maximum]``. Raises\n nothing; an unusable value is logged and the default is used so a typo in\n deployment configuration cannot take the service down.\n \"\"\"\n raw = _get(env, name, default)\n try:\n value = int(raw)\n except ValueError:\n logger.warning(\"Invalid integer for %s; using default %s\", name, default)\n value = int(default)\n if value < minimum or value > maximum:\n logger.warning(\n \"Value for %s outside [%d, %d]; using default %s\",\n name,\n minimum,\n maximum,\n default,\n )\n value = int(default)\n return value\n\n\ndef _get_bool_default_true(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Read a boolean setting that defaults to true.\n\n Returns ``False`` only for the case-insensitive values ``false``, ``0`` or\n ``no``; every other value (including absence) yields ``True``. Raises\n nothing.\n \"\"\"\n raw = _get(env, name, \"true\").lower()\n return raw not in _FALSE_VALUES\n\n\ndef _get_bool_default_false(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Read a boolean setting that defaults to false.\n\n Returns ``True`` only for the case-insensitive values ``true``, ``1`` or\n ``yes``; every other value (including absence) yields ``False``. Raises\n nothing.\n \"\"\"\n raw = _get(env, name, \"false\").lower()\n return raw in _TRUE_VALUES\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Settings:\n \"\"\"Immutable snapshot of the service configuration.\"\"\"\n\n db_path: str\n base_url: str\n default_ttl_days: int\n max_url_length: int\n code_length: int\n code_max_attempts: int\n rate_limit_max: int\n rate_limit_window_seconds: int\n rate_limit_enabled: bool\n trust_forwarded_for: bool\n stats_default_limit: int\n stats_max_limit: int\n dns_resolution_enabled: bool\n log_level: str\n\n @classmethod\n def from_env(cls, env: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None) -> \"Settings\":\n \"\"\"Build a :class:`Settings` instance from the process environment.\n\n ``env`` defaults to :data:`os.environ`. Returns a fully populated,\n range-checked settings object. Raises nothing: invalid values fall back\n to the documented defaults.\n \"\"\"\n source: Mapping[str, str] = os.environ if env is None else env\n\n db_path = _get(source, \"LINKS_DB_PATH\", \"./links.db\")\n base_url = _get(source, \"LINKS_BASE_URL\", \"http://localhost:8000\").rstrip(\"/\")\n if len(base_url) > MAX_BASE_URL_LENGTH:\n logger.warning(\"LINKS_BASE_URL too long; using default\")\n base_url = \"http://localhost:8000\"\n\n max_url_length = _get_int(\n source, \"LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH\", \"2048\", 1, ABSOLUTE_MAX_URL_LENGTH\n )\n stats_max_limit = _get_int(source, \"LINKS_STATS_MAX_LIMIT\", \"500\", 1, 10000)\n stats_default_limit = _get_int(\n source, \"LINKS_STATS_DEFAULT_LIMIT\", \"50\", 1, 10000\n )\n if stats_default_limit > stats_max_limit:\n stats_default_limit = stats_max_limit\n\n log_level = _get(source, \"LINKS_LOG_LEVEL\", \"INFO\").upper()\n if log_level not in _VALID_LOG_LEVELS:\n log_level = \"INFO\"\n\n return cls(\n db_path=db_path,\n base_url=base_url,\n default_ttl_days=_get_int(\n source, \"LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_DAYS\", \"30\", 1, 36500\n ),\n max_url_length=max_url_length,\n code_length=_get_int(source, \"LINKS_CODE_LENGTH\", \"7\", 4, 32),\n code_max_attempts=_get_int(\n source, \"LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS\", \"5\", 1, 100\n ),\n rate_limit_max=_get_int(source, \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX\", \"10\", 1, 1000000),\n rate_limit_window_seconds=_get_int(\n source, \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS\", \"60\", 1, 86400\n ),\n rate_limit_enabled=_get_bool_default_true(\n source, \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED\"\n ),\n trust_forwarded_for=_get_bool_default_false(\n source, \"LINKS_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR\"\n ),\n stats_default_limit=stats_default_limit,\n stats_max_limit=stats_max_limit,\n dns_resolution_enabled=_get_bool_default_true(\n source, \"LINKS_DNS_RESOLUTION_ENABLED\"\n ),\n log_level=log_level,\n )\n\n\n--- app/db.py ---\n\"\"\"SQLite access helpers.\n\nOne connection per request; WAL mode so a click insert does not block\nconcurrent redirect reads. Every statement in the service is parameterized.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(\"links.db\")\n\nSCHEMA_STATEMENTS = (\n \"\"\"\n CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (\n id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n url TEXT NOT NULL,\n created_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n expires_at TEXT NOT NULL\n )\n \"\"\",\n \"\"\"\n CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clicks (\n id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n link_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES links(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n clicked_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n referrer TEXT,\n user_agent TEXT\n )\n \"\"\",\n \"\"\"\n CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_clicks_link_time\n ON clicks(link_id, clicked_at DESC, id DESC)\n \"\"\",\n)\n\n\ndef connect(db_path: str) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n \"\"\"Open a configured SQLite connection.\n\n ``db_path`` is the database file path. Returns a connection with\n ``sqlite3.Row`` rows, foreign keys enforced, WAL journalling and a 5 second\n busy timeout. Raises :class:`sqlite3.Error` when the database cannot be\n opened.\n \"\"\"\n conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0)\n conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n conn.execute(\"PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000\")\n conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n try:\n conn.execute(\"PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL\")\n except sqlite3.DatabaseError: # pragma: no cover - filesystem dependent\n logger.warning(\"WAL journal mode unavailable; continuing with default\")\n conn.execute(\"PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL\")\n return conn\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef get_connection(db_path: str) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n \"\"\"Context manager yielding a configured SQLite connection.\n\n ``db_path`` is the database file path. Yields the connection and always\n closes it. Raises :class:`sqlite3.Error` when the database cannot be\n opened.\n \"\"\"\n conn = connect(db_path)\n try:\n yield conn\n finally:\n conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db(db_path: str) -> None:\n \"\"\"Create the schema if it does not exist.\n\n ``db_path`` is the database file path; its parent directory is created when\n missing. Returns nothing. Raises :class:`sqlite3.Error` or :class:`OSError`\n when the database or its directory cannot be created.\n \"\"\"\n parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(db_path))\n if parent:\n os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)\n with get_connection(db_path) as conn:\n for statement in SCHEMA_STATEMENTS:\n conn.execute(statement)\n conn.commit()\n\n\n--- app/errors.py ---\n\"\"\"Stable error envelope shared by every endpoint.\n\nAll failures are rendered as ``{\"error\": {\"code\": ..., \"message\": ...}}``.\nNo stack trace, database message or filesystem path is ever placed in a\nresponse body.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, Mapping, Optional\n\nfrom fastapi.responses import JSONResponse\n\nMAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 400\n\n\nclass ApiError(Exception):\n \"\"\"Application level error carrying an HTTP status and a stable code.\"\"\"\n\n def __init__(\n self,\n status_code: int,\n code: str,\n message: str,\n headers: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,\n ) -> None:\n \"\"\"Create an API error.\n\n ``status_code`` is the HTTP status to return, ``code`` the stable\n machine readable identifier, ``message`` a human readable, non\n sensitive explanation and ``headers`` optional extra response headers.\n Returns nothing. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n super().__init__(message)\n self.status_code = status_code\n self.code = code\n self.message = message[:MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH]\n self.headers: Dict[str, str] = dict(headers or {})\n\n\ndef error_payload(code: str, message: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n \"\"\"Build the canonical error body.\n\n Returns a dict of the shape ``{\"error\": {\"code\": ..., \"message\": ...}}``.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return {\"error\": {\"code\": code, \"message\": message[:MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH]}}\n\n\ndef error_response(\n status_code: int,\n code: str,\n message: str,\n headers: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,\n) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Build a JSON error response using the canonical envelope.\n\n Returns a :class:`fastapi.responses.JSONResponse` with ``status_code`` and\n the given headers. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return JSONResponse(\n status_code=status_code,\n content=error_payload(code, message),\n headers=dict(headers or {}),\n )\n\n\n--- app/main.py ---\n\"\"\"FastAPI application for the URL shortener service.\n\nEndpoints:\n POST /api/links create a short link\n GET /api/links/{code}/stats per-link click analytics\n GET /health liveness probe\n GET /{code} redirect to the stored destination\n\nThe redirect destination always comes from the validated, stored row; it can\nnever come from a query parameter, header or path segment of the request.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\nfrom datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone\nfrom typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Dict, List, Optional\nfrom urllib.parse import quote\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Request, Response\nfrom fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError\nfrom fastapi.responses import JSONResponse\nfrom starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException\n\nfrom . import codes as codes_module\nfrom .config import Settings\nfrom .db import get_connection, init_db\nfrom .errors import ApiError, error_response\nfrom .models import CreateLinkRequest, CreateLinkResponse, HealthResponse, StatsResponse\nfrom .ratelimit import RateLimitMiddleware\nfrom .validation import validate_destination_url\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(\"links\")\n\nTIMESTAMP_FORMAT = \"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ\"\nMAX_HEADER_STORE_LENGTH = 2048\n_LOCATION_SAFE_CHARACTERS = \":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;=%~-._\"\n\n\nclass ClientAddressRedactionFilter(logging.Filter):\n \"\"\"Logging filter that removes the client address from access log records.\"\"\"\n\n def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Replace the client address argument of an access log record.\n\n ``record`` is the log record being emitted. Returns ``True`` so the\n record is always kept, after blanking the first positional argument\n which uvicorn uses for the client address. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if isinstance(record.args, tuple) and record.args:\n record.args = (\"-\",) + tuple(record.args[1:])\n return True\n\n\ndef configure_logging(level: str) -> None:\n \"\"\"Configure root logging and strip client addresses from access logs.\n\n ``level`` is a logging level name such as ``INFO``. Returns nothing. Raises\n nothing.\n \"\"\"\n numeric = getattr(logging, level.upper(), logging.INFO)\n logging.basicConfig(\n level=numeric,\n format=\"%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s\",\n )\n logging.getLogger().setLevel(numeric)\n access_logger = logging.getLogger(\"uvicorn.access\")\n if not any(\n isinstance(existing, ClientAddressRedactionFilter)\n for existing in access_logger.filters\n ):\n access_logger.addFilter(ClientAddressRedactionFilter())\n\n\ndef format_timestamp(value: datetime) -> str:\n \"\"\"Render an aware datetime in the fixed stored UTC format.\n\n ``value`` is a timezone aware datetime (naive input is treated as UTC).\n Returns a string like ``2024-01-31T12:00:00.000000Z``. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if value.tzinfo is None:\n value = value.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n return value.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime(TIMESTAMP_FORMAT)\n\n\ndef parse_timestamp(value: str) -> datetime:\n \"\"\"Parse a stored timestamp back into an aware UTC datetime.\n\n ``value`` is a stored timestamp string. Returns an aware UTC datetime.\n Raises :class:`ValueError` when the string cannot be parsed.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n return datetime.strptime(value, TIMESTAMP_FORMAT).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n except ValueError:\n pass\n text = value.strip()\n if text.endswith((\"Z\", \"z\")):\n text = text[:-1] + \"+00:00\"\n parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(text)\n if parsed.tzinfo is None:\n parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n return parsed.astimezone(timezone.utc)\n\n\ndef parse_client_expiry(raw: str) -> datetime:\n \"\"\"Parse a client supplied ISO-8601 expiry into an aware UTC datetime.\n\n ``raw`` is the ``expires_at`` value from the request body. Returns the\n instant normalized to UTC. Raises :class:`app.errors.ApiError` with status\n 400 and code ``invalid_expiry`` when the value is not a valid ISO-8601\n timestamp.\n \"\"\"\n text = raw.strip()\n if not text:\n raise ApiError(\n 400, \"invalid_expiry\", \"expires_at must be a valid ISO-8601 timestamp.\"\n )\n candidate = text[:-1] + \"+00:00\" if text.endswith((\"Z\", \"z\")) else text\n try:\n parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(candidate)\n except ValueError:\n raise ApiError(\n 400, \"invalid_expiry\", \"expires_at must be a valid ISO-8601 timestamp.\"\n )\n if parsed.tzinfo is None:\n parsed = parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n return parsed.astimezone(timezone.utc)\n\n\ndef generate_code(length: int) -> str:\n \"\"\"Generate a CSPRNG short code.\n\n ``length`` is the number of base62 characters. Returns the generated code.\n Raises :class:`ValueError` when ``length`` is not positive.\n \"\"\"\n return codes_module.generate_code(length)\n\n\ndef clip_header(value: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:\n \"\"\"Truncate a header value for storage.\n\n ``value`` is a header value or ``None``. Returns the value truncated to\n 2048 characters, or ``None`` when the header was absent. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if value is None:\n return None\n return value[:MAX_HEADER_STORE_LENGTH]\n\n\ndef location_header_value(url: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Render a stored URL as a Location header value.\n\n ``url`` is the stored destination. Returns the URL byte-for-byte when it is\n ASCII, otherwise a percent-encoded form so the header stays transmittable.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if url.isascii():\n return url\n return quote(url, safe=_LOCATION_SAFE_CHARACTERS)\n\n\ndef create_app(settings: Optional[Settings] = None) -> FastAPI:\n \"\"\"Build the FastAPI application.\n\n ``settings`` overrides the environment derived configuration when given.\n Returns a fully wired :class:`fastapi.FastAPI` instance with the schema\n created. Raises nothing; a failure to create the schema at build time is\n logged and retried at startup and on each request.\n \"\"\"\n resolved = settings if settings is not None else Settings.from_env()\n configure_logging(resolved.log_level)\n\n try:\n init_db(resolved.db_path)\n except (sqlite3.Error, OSError):\n logger.warning(\"Database initialisation deferred to startup\", exc_info=True)\n\n @asynccontextmanager\n async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:\n \"\"\"Create the schema at startup.\n\n Yields control to the running application. Raises nothing; database\n problems are logged and surfaced by the health endpoint.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n init_db(resolved.db_path)\n except (sqlite3.Error, OSError):\n logger.error(\"Database initialisation failed at startup\", exc_info=True)\n yield\n\n app = FastAPI(\n title=\"URL Shortener\",\n version=\"1.0.0\",\n description=\"Short links with expiry and IP-free click analytics.\",\n lifespan=lifespan,\n )\n app.state.settings = resolved\n app.state.code_pattern = re.compile(r\"^[A-Za-z0-9]{%d}$\" % resolved.code_length)\n app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware, settings=resolved)\n\n # ---------------------------------------------------------------- errors\n\n @app.exception_handler(ApiError)\n async def handle_api_error(_: Request, exc: ApiError) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render an :class:`ApiError` using the stable envelope.\n\n Returns the JSON error response with the error's status and headers.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return error_response(exc.status_code, exc.code, exc.message, exc.headers)\n\n @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)\n async def handle_validation_error(\n _: Request, exc: RequestValidationError\n ) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render a request validation failure as 422 ``validation_error``.\n\n Returns the JSON error response. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n details: List[str] = []\n for error in exc.errors()[:5]:\n location = \".\".join(\n str(part) for part in error.get(\"loc\", ()) if part != \"body\"\n )\n details.append(f\"{location or 'body'}: {error.get('msg', 'invalid value')}\")\n message = \"Request validation failed.\"\n if details:\n message = f\"{message} {'; '.join(details)}\"\n return error_response(422, \"validation_error\", message)\n\n @app.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)\n async def handle_http_exception(\n _: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException\n ) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render framework HTTP exceptions using the stable envelope.\n\n Returns the JSON error response. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if exc.status_code == 404:\n code = \"not_found\"\n message = \"The requested resource does not exist.\"\n elif exc.status_code == 405:\n code = \"method_not_allowed\"\n message = \"The HTTP method is not allowed for this resource.\"\n else:\n code = \"http_error\"\n message = \"The request could not be completed.\"\n headers = dict(getattr(exc, \"headers\", None) or {})\n return error_response(exc.status_code, code, message, headers)\n\n @app.exception_handler(sqlite3.Error)\n async def handle_database_error(_: Request, __: sqlite3.Error) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render a database failure as 503 without leaking driver detail.\n\n Returns the JSON error response. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n logger.error(\"Database error while handling request\", exc_info=True)\n return error_response(\n 503,\n \"service_unavailable\",\n \"The service is temporarily unable to handle the request.\",\n )\n\n @app.exception_handler(Exception)\n async def handle_unexpected_error(_: Request, __: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render an unexpected failure as a generic 500.\n\n Returns the JSON error response with no internal detail. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n logger.error(\"Unhandled error while handling request\", exc_info=True)\n return error_response(\n 500, \"internal_error\", \"An unexpected error occurred.\"\n )\n\n # ---------------------------------------------------------------- routes\n\n @app.get(\"/health\", response_model=HealthResponse, tags=[\"system\"])\n def health(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Report liveness without reading any user data.\n\n Returns ``{\"status\": \"ok\"}`` with 200 when SQLite answers ``SELECT 1``,\n or ``{\"status\": \"degraded\"}`` with 503 otherwise. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n current: Settings = request.app.state.settings\n try:\n with get_connection(current.db_path) as conn:\n conn.execute(\"SELECT 1\").fetchone()\n except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - health must never raise\n logger.warning(\"Health check failed\", exc_info=True)\n return JSONResponse(status_code=503, content={\"status\": \"degraded\"})\n return JSONResponse(status_code=200, content={\"status\": \"ok\"})\n\n @app.post(\n \"/api/links\",\n status_code=201,\n response_model=CreateLinkResponse,\n tags=[\"links\"],\n )\n def create_link(payload: CreateLinkRequest, request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n \"\"\"Create a short link for a validated public http(s) destination.\n\n ``payload`` is the validated request body. Returns the created link\n representation (code, short_url, url, created_at, expires_at). Raises\n :class:`ApiError` 422 ``validation_error`` for an over-long or blank\n url, 400 ``unsupported_scheme`` / ``invalid_url`` / ``blocked_destination``\n for a rejected destination, 400 ``invalid_expiry`` for a bad expiry, and\n 503 ``code_generation_failed`` when no unique code could be allocated.\n \"\"\"\n current: Settings = request.app.state.settings\n url = payload.url\n if len(url) > current.max_url_length:\n raise ApiError(\n 422,\n \"validation_error\",\n f\"url must be at most {current.max_url_length} characters.\",\n )\n if not url.strip():\n raise ApiError(422, \"validation_error\", \"url must not be empty.\")\n\n validate_destination_url(url, dns_enabled=current.dns_resolution_enabled)\n\n now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n if payload.expires_at is None:\n expires = now + timedelta(days=current.default_ttl_days)\n else:\n expires = parse_client_expiry(payload.expires_at)\n if expires <= now:\n raise ApiError(\n 400, \"invalid_expiry\", \"expires_at must be in the future.\"\n )\n\n created_text = format_timestamp(now)\n expires_text = format_timestamp(expires)\n\n code: Optional[str] = None\n with get_connection(current.db_path) as conn:\n for _ in range(current.code_max_attempts):\n candidate = generate_code(current.code_length)\n try:\n conn.execute(\n \"INSERT INTO links (code, url, created_at, expires_at) \"\n \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n (candidate, url, created_text, expires_text),\n )\n conn.commit()\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n conn.rollback()\n continue\n code = candidate\n break\n\n if code is None:\n raise ApiError(\n 503,\n \"code_generation_failed\",\n \"Could not allocate a unique short code. Please retry.\",\n )\n\n return {\n \"code\": code,\n \"short_url\": f\"{current.base_url}/{code}\",\n \"url\": url,\n \"created_at\": created_text,\n \"expires_at\": expires_text,\n }\n\n @app.get(\n \"/api/links/{code}/stats\",\n response_model=StatsResponse,\n tags=[\"links\"],\n )\n def link_stats(\n code: str,\n request: Request,\n limit: Optional[int] = Query(default=None, description=\"Clicks per page.\"),\n offset: int = Query(default=0, description=\"Clicks to skip.\"),\n ) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n \"\"\"Return per-link analytics, including for expired links.\n\n ``code`` identifies the link; ``limit`` and ``offset`` page the newest\n first clicks array. Returns the link metadata, the total click count and\n the requested page of clicks. Raises :class:`ApiError` 404 ``not_found``\n for an unknown code and 422 ``validation_error`` for out of range\n pagination parameters.\n \"\"\"\n current: Settings = request.app.state.settings\n pattern: re.Pattern[str] = request.app.state.code_pattern\n if not pattern.match(code):\n raise ApiError(404, \"not_found\", \"No link exists for that code.\")\n\n effective_limit = current.stats_default_limit if limit is None else limit\n if effective_limit < 1 or effective_limit > current.stats_max_limit:\n raise ApiError(\n 422,\n \"validation_error\",\n f\"limit must be between 1 and {current.stats_max_limit}.\",\n )\n if offset < 0:\n raise ApiError(422, \"validation_error\", \"offset must be zero or greater.\")\n\n with get_connection(current.db_path) as conn:\n link_row = conn.execute(\n \"SELECT id, code, url, created_at, expires_at FROM links \"\n \"WHERE code = ?\",\n (code,),\n ).fetchone()\n if link_row is None:\n raise ApiError(404, \"not_found\", \"No link exists for that code.\")\n total_row = conn.execute(\n \"SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM clicks WHERE link_id = ?\",\n (link_row[\"id\"],),\n ).fetchone()\n click_rows = conn.execute(\n \"SELECT clicked_at, referrer, user_agent FROM clicks \"\n \"WHERE link_id = ? ORDER BY clicked_at DESC, id DESC \"\n \"LIMIT ? OFFSET ?\",\n (link_row[\"id\"], effective_limit, offset),\n ).fetchall()\n\n clicks = [\n {\n \"timestamp\": row[\"clicked_at\"],\n \"referrer\": row[\"referrer\"],\n \"user_agent\": row[\"user_agent\"],\n }\n for row in click_rows\n ]\n return {\n \"code\": link_row[\"code\"],\n \"url\": link_row[\"url\"],\n \"created_at\": link_row[\"created_at\"],\n \"expires_at\": link_row[\"expires_at\"],\n \"total_clicks\": int(total_row[\"total\"]) if total_row else 0,\n \"clicks\": clicks,\n }\n\n @app.get(\"/{code}\", include_in_schema=False)\n def redirect_to_target(code: str, request: Request) -> Response:\n \"\"\"Redirect a visitor to the stored destination and record the click.\n\n ``code`` is the short code from the path; the destination is read from\n the stored, previously validated row and never from request input.\n Returns a 307 response whose Location is the stored URL, with\n ``Cache-Control: no-store``. Raises :class:`ApiError` 404 ``not_found``\n for unknown or malformed codes and 410 ``link_expired`` for lapsed\n links; neither writes a click row.\n \"\"\"\n current: Settings = request.app.state.settings\n pattern: re.Pattern[str] = request.app.state.code_pattern\n if not pattern.match(code):\n raise ApiError(404, \"not_found\", \"No link exists for that code.\")\n\n now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n with get_connection(current.db_path) as conn:\n row = conn.execute(\n \"SELECT id, url, expires_at FROM links WHERE code = ?\",\n (code,),\n ).fetchone()\n if row is None:\n raise ApiError(404, \"not_found\", \"No link exists for that code.\")\n\n try:\n expires = parse_timestamp(row[\"expires_at\"])\n except ValueError:\n # Fail closed: an unreadable expiry is treated as expired.\n logger.error(\"Unparsable expires_at for a stored link\")\n raise ApiError(410, \"link_expired\", \"This link has expired.\")\n\n if now >= expires:\n raise ApiError(410, \"link_expired\", \"This link has expired.\")\n\n conn.execute(\n \"INSERT INTO clicks (link_id, clicked_at, referrer, user_agent) \"\n \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n (\n row[\"id\"],\n format_timestamp(now),\n clip_header(request.headers.get(\"referer\")),\n clip_header(request.headers.get(\"user-agent\")),\n ),\n )\n conn.commit()\n destination = row[\"url\"]\n\n return Response(\n status_code=307,\n headers={\n \"Location\": location_header_value(destination),\n \"Cache-Control\": \"no-store\",\n \"Referrer-Policy\": \"no-referrer\",\n },\n )\n\n return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\": # pragma: no cover - manual entry point\n import uvicorn\n\n uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", host=\"127.0.0.1\", port=8000, reload=False)\n\n\n--- app/models.py ---\n\"\"\"Typed request and response models validated at the HTTP boundary.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import List, Optional\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, StringConstraints\nfrom typing_extensions import Annotated\n\nfrom .config import ABSOLUTE_MAX_URL_LENGTH, MAX_EXPIRES_AT_LENGTH\n\nUrlStr = Annotated[\n str,\n StringConstraints(strict=True, min_length=1, max_length=ABSOLUTE_MAX_URL_LENGTH),\n]\n\nExpiryStr = Annotated[\n str,\n StringConstraints(strict=True, min_length=1, max_length=MAX_EXPIRES_AT_LENGTH),\n]\n\n\nclass CreateLinkRequest(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body of ``POST /api/links``.\"\"\"\n\n model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n url: UrlStr = Field(\n ...,\n description=\"Public http(s) destination URL to shorten.\",\n )\n expires_at: Optional[ExpiryStr] = Field(\n default=None,\n description=\"Optional ISO-8601 expiry instant; must be in the future.\",\n )\n\n\nclass CreateLinkResponse(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body returned by a successful ``POST /api/links``.\"\"\"\n\n code: str\n short_url: str\n url: str\n created_at: str\n expires_at: str\n\n\nclass ClickEntry(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"A single recorded redirect, free of any client address.\"\"\"\n\n timestamp: str\n referrer: Optional[str] = None\n user_agent: Optional[str] = None\n\n\nclass StatsResponse(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body returned by ``GET /api/links/{code}/stats``.\"\"\"\n\n code: str\n url: str\n created_at: str\n expires_at: str\n total_clicks: int\n clicks: List[ClickEntry]\n\n\nclass HealthResponse(BaseModel):\n \"\"\"Body returned by ``GET /health``.\"\"\"\n\n status: str\n\n\n--- app/ratelimit.py ---\n\"\"\"In-process sliding window rate limiting, applied as ASGI middleware.\n\nThe limiter runs before routing and body parsing, so a flood is rejected\nwithout touching the database. Keys are a per-boot salted SHA-256 of the client\naddress: the address itself is never stored, persisted or logged, and all state\nvanishes on restart.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hashlib\nimport math\nimport re\nimport secrets\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom collections import OrderedDict, deque\nfrom typing import Deque, Optional, Tuple\n\nfrom starlette.types import ASGIApp, Receive, Scope, Send\n\nfrom .config import Settings\nfrom .errors import error_response\n\n#: Redirects are far cheaper and far more frequent than creations, so the\n#: redirect bucket uses a multiple of the configured creation budget. The\n#: design pins only the creation limit; this keeps redirects protected without\n#: introducing a new environment variable.\nREDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER = 100\n\n#: Upper bound on tracked keys so the limiter cannot grow without limit.\nMAX_TRACKED_KEYS = 20000\n\nCREATE_PATH = \"/api/links\"\n\n\nclass RateLimitMiddleware:\n \"\"\"Rate limit link creation and redirects in a single place.\"\"\"\n\n def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, settings: Settings) -> None:\n \"\"\"Wrap an ASGI application with the limiter.\n\n ``app`` is the downstream ASGI application and ``settings`` the service\n configuration. Returns nothing. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n self.app = app\n self.settings = settings\n self._salt = secrets.token_bytes(32)\n self._lock = threading.Lock()\n self._hits: \"OrderedDict[str, Deque[float]]\" = OrderedDict()\n self._code_pattern = re.compile(\n r\"^/[A-Za-z0-9]{%d}$\" % settings.code_length\n )\n\n async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:\n \"\"\"ASGI entry point.\n\n ``scope``, ``receive`` and ``send`` are the standard ASGI arguments.\n Returns nothing; either forwards the call downstream or emits a 429 with\n a ``Retry-After`` header. Raises nothing of its own.\n \"\"\"\n if scope.get(\"type\") != \"http\" or not self.settings.rate_limit_enabled:\n await self.app(scope, receive, send)\n return\n\n rule = self._rule_for(str(scope.get(\"method\", \"\")), str(scope.get(\"path\", \"\")))\n if rule is None:\n await self.app(scope, receive, send)\n return\n\n bucket, limit = rule\n allowed, retry_after = self._consume(bucket, self._client_key(scope, bucket), limit)\n if allowed:\n await self.app(scope, receive, send)\n return\n\n response = error_response(\n 429,\n \"rate_limited\",\n \"Too many requests. Please retry later.\",\n headers={\"Retry-After\": str(retry_after), \"Cache-Control\": \"no-store\"},\n )\n await response(scope, receive, send)\n\n def _rule_for(self, method: str, path: str) -> Optional[Tuple[str, int]]:\n \"\"\"Decide which limiter bucket applies to a request.\n\n ``method`` is the HTTP method and ``path`` the request path. Returns a\n ``(bucket, limit)`` pair for rate limited routes, or ``None`` when the\n route is not limited. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n normalized = path.rstrip(\"/\") or \"/\"\n if method.upper() == \"POST\" and normalized == CREATE_PATH:\n return \"create\", self.settings.rate_limit_max\n if method.upper() in {\"GET\", \"HEAD\"} and self._code_pattern.match(path):\n return \"redirect\", self.settings.rate_limit_max * REDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER\n return None\n\n def _client_address(self, scope: Scope) -> str:\n \"\"\"Determine the client address used for keying.\n\n ``scope`` is the ASGI scope. Returns the first ``X-Forwarded-For`` entry\n when the service is configured to trust it, otherwise the peer address,\n or ``\"unknown\"``. The value is only hashed, never stored or logged.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if self.settings.trust_forwarded_for:\n for name, value in scope.get(\"headers\") or []:\n if name == b\"x-forwarded-for\":\n first = value.decode(\"latin-1\", \"ignore\").split(\",\")[0].strip()\n if first:\n return first[:128]\n break\n client = scope.get(\"client\")\n if client:\n try:\n return str(client[0])[:128]\n except (IndexError, TypeError): # pragma: no cover - defensive\n return \"unknown\"\n return \"unknown\"\n\n def _client_key(self, scope: Scope, bucket: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Build the salted hash key for a client and bucket.\n\n ``scope`` is the ASGI scope and ``bucket`` the limiter bucket name.\n Returns a hex SHA-256 digest that cannot be reversed to an IP address.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n digest = hashlib.sha256()\n digest.update(self._salt)\n digest.update(bucket.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n digest.update(b\"\\x00\")\n digest.update(self._client_address(scope).encode(\"utf-8\", \"ignore\"))\n return digest.hexdigest()\n\n def _consume(self, bucket: str, key: str, limit: int) -> Tuple[bool, int]:\n \"\"\"Record a request against the rolling window.\n\n ``bucket`` is the limiter bucket (used only for readability), ``key``\n the hashed client key and ``limit`` the allowed number of requests per\n window. Returns ``(allowed, retry_after_seconds)`` where\n ``retry_after_seconds`` is at least 1 when the request is denied.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n now = time.monotonic()\n window = float(self.settings.rate_limit_window_seconds)\n with self._lock:\n hits = self._hits.get(key)\n if hits is None:\n hits = deque()\n self._hits[key] = hits\n self._hits.move_to_end(key)\n while hits and (now - hits[0]) >= window:\n hits.popleft()\n if len(hits) >= limit:\n retry_after = max(1, math.ceil(window - (now - hits[0])))\n return False, retry_after\n hits.append(now)\n self._prune_locked()\n return True, 0\n\n def _prune_locked(self) -> None:\n \"\"\"Drop stale limiter state while the lock is held.\n\n Returns nothing. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if len(self._hits) <= MAX_TRACKED_KEYS:\n return\n for stale_key in [k for k, v in self._hits.items() if not v]:\n self._hits.pop(stale_key, None)\n while len(self._hits) > MAX_TRACKED_KEYS:\n self._hits.popitem(last=False)\n\n\n--- app/validation.py ---\n\"\"\"Destination URL validation.\n\nOnly ``http`` and ``https`` URLs are accepted (allow-list, not a block-list of\nbad schemes). Hosts are resolved and every resulting address is checked against\nthe denied ranges: loopback, private, link-local (including the cloud metadata\naddress 169.254.169.254), unique-local, CGNAT, multicast, unspecified and\nother reserved space. No HTTP request is ever made to a user supplied URL.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport ipaddress\nimport logging\nimport socket\nfrom typing import List, Optional, Tuple, Union\nfrom urllib.parse import urlsplit\n\nfrom .errors import ApiError\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(\"links.validation\")\n\nIPAddress = Union[ipaddress.IPv4Address, ipaddress.IPv6Address]\nIPNetwork = Union[ipaddress.IPv4Network, ipaddress.IPv6Network]\n\nALLOWED_SCHEMES = frozenset({\"http\", \"https\"})\nMAX_HOST_LENGTH = 253\n\nBLOCKED_MESSAGE = (\n \"The destination host is not a permitted public address.\"\n)\n\n#: Explicitly denied singleton addresses. 169.254.169.254 is the cloud\n#: metadata endpoint; reaching it turns a URL fetcher into a credential leak.\nCLOUD_METADATA_ADDRESSES = frozenset(\n {\n ipaddress.ip_address(\"169.254.169.254\"),\n ipaddress.ip_address(\"fd00:ec2::254\"),\n }\n)\n\nBLOCKED_NETWORKS: Tuple[IPNetwork, ...] = (\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"0.0.0.0/8\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"10.0.0.0/8\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"100.64.0.0/10\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"127.0.0.0/8\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"169.254.0.0/16\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"172.16.0.0/12\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"192.0.0.0/24\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"192.0.2.0/24\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"192.168.0.0/16\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"198.18.0.0/15\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"198.51.100.0/24\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"203.0.113.0/24\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"224.0.0.0/4\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"240.0.0.0/4\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"255.255.255.255/32\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"::/128\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"::1/128\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"64:ff9b:1::/48\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"100::/64\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"2001:db8::/32\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"fc00::/7\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"fe80::/10\"),\n ipaddress.ip_network(\"ff00::/8\"),\n)\n\n\ndef _parse_int_token(token: str) -> Optional[int]:\n \"\"\"Parse one dotted-quad component allowing decimal, octal and hex forms.\n\n ``token`` is a single component such as ``0x7f``, ``0177`` or ``127``.\n Returns the integer value, or ``None`` when the token is not a valid\n numeric component. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not token:\n return None\n lowered = token.lower()\n try:\n if lowered.startswith(\"0x\"):\n digits = lowered[2:]\n if not digits or any(c not in \"0123456789abcdef\" for c in digits):\n return None\n value = int(digits, 16)\n elif len(lowered) > 1 and lowered.startswith(\"0\"):\n digits = lowered[1:]\n if any(c not in \"01234567\" for c in digits):\n return None\n value = int(digits, 8)\n else:\n if not lowered.isdigit():\n return None\n value = int(lowered, 10)\n except ValueError:\n return None\n if value < 0 or value > 0xFFFFFFFF:\n return None\n return value\n\n\ndef parse_relaxed_ipv4(host: str) -> Optional[ipaddress.IPv4Address]:\n \"\"\"Decode non canonical IPv4 literals (decimal, octal, hex, short forms).\n\n ``host`` is the host component of a URL. Returns the decoded\n :class:`ipaddress.IPv4Address` when the host is any ``inet_aton`` style\n literal such as ``2130706433``, ``0x7f.0.0.1`` or ``127.1``; returns\n ``None`` when the host is not such a literal. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n candidate = host.rstrip(\".\")\n if not candidate:\n return None\n parts = candidate.split(\".\")\n if len(parts) > 4:\n return None\n values: List[int] = []\n for part in parts:\n parsed = _parse_int_token(part)\n if parsed is None:\n return None\n values.append(parsed)\n for value in values[:-1]:\n if value > 0xFF:\n return None\n remaining_bytes = 4 - (len(values) - 1)\n last = values[-1]\n if last > (256 ** remaining_bytes) - 1:\n return None\n total = 0\n for index, value in enumerate(values[:-1]):\n total |= value << (8 * (3 - index))\n total |= last\n try:\n return ipaddress.IPv4Address(total)\n except (ipaddress.AddressValueError, ValueError):\n return None\n\n\ndef parse_host_as_ip(host: str) -> Optional[IPAddress]:\n \"\"\"Interpret a URL host as an IP literal if possible.\n\n ``host`` is the (already bracket stripped) host component. Returns the\n parsed address for canonical IPv4/IPv6 literals and for relaxed IPv4\n literals, or ``None`` when the host is a name. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n cleaned = host.strip().strip(\"[]\")\n if not cleaned:\n return None\n if \"%\" in cleaned:\n cleaned = cleaned.split(\"%\", 1)[0]\n try:\n return ipaddress.ip_address(cleaned)\n except ValueError:\n pass\n return parse_relaxed_ipv4(cleaned)\n\n\ndef _embedded_addresses(ip: IPAddress) -> List[IPAddress]:\n \"\"\"Extract IPv4 addresses embedded inside an IPv6 address.\n\n ``ip`` is any parsed address. Returns a list of embedded IPv4 addresses for\n IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, 6to4 and Teredo forms; an empty list when\n nothing is embedded. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not isinstance(ip, ipaddress.IPv6Address):\n return []\n embedded: List[IPAddress] = []\n if ip.ipv4_mapped is not None:\n embedded.append(ip.ipv4_mapped)\n if ip.sixtofour is not None:\n embedded.append(ip.sixtofour)\n teredo = ip.teredo\n if teredo is not None:\n embedded.extend([teredo[0], teredo[1]])\n packed = ip.packed\n if packed[:12] == b\"\\x00\" * 12 and int(ip) > 1:\n embedded.append(ipaddress.IPv4Address(packed[12:]))\n return embedded\n\n\ndef _single_address_blocked(ip: IPAddress) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Test one address (without unwrapping) against the denied ranges.\n\n ``ip`` is a parsed address. Returns ``True`` when the address is denied.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if ip in CLOUD_METADATA_ADDRESSES:\n return True\n if (\n ip.is_loopback\n or ip.is_private\n or ip.is_link_local\n or ip.is_multicast\n or ip.is_unspecified\n or ip.is_reserved\n ):\n return True\n if not ip.is_global:\n return True\n for network in BLOCKED_NETWORKS:\n if ip.version == network.version and ip in network:\n return True\n return False\n\n\ndef is_blocked_address(ip: IPAddress) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Test an address, including any embedded IPv4 form, against the denylist.\n\n ``ip`` is a parsed address. Returns ``True`` when the address itself or any\n address embedded within it is loopback, private, link-local, unique-local,\n CGNAT, multicast, unspecified or otherwise reserved. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if _single_address_blocked(ip):\n return True\n for embedded in _embedded_addresses(ip):\n if _single_address_blocked(embedded):\n return True\n return False\n\n\ndef resolve_host(host: str) -> List[str]:\n \"\"\"Resolve a hostname to textual addresses using the stdlib resolver.\n\n ``host`` is a DNS name. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n infos = socket.getaddrinfo(\n host, None, family=socket.AF_UNSPEC, type=socket.SOCK_STREAM\n )\n except (socket.gaierror, UnicodeError, OSError, ValueError):\n return []\n addresses: List[str] = []\n for info in infos:\n address: Optional[str] = None\n if isinstance(info, str):\n address = info\n else:\n try:\n sockaddr = info[4]\n except (IndexError, TypeError, KeyError):\n sockaddr = None\n if isinstance(sockaddr, (tuple, list)) and sockaddr:\n candidate = sockaddr[0]\n if isinstance(candidate, bytes):\n candidate = candidate.decode(\"ascii\", \"ignore\")\n if isinstance(candidate, str):\n address = candidate\n elif isinstance(sockaddr, str):\n address = sockaddr\n if not address:\n continue\n addresses.append(address.split(\"%\", 1)[0])\n return addresses\n\n\ndef _has_forbidden_characters(url: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Detect control characters or whitespace inside a URL.\n\n ``url`` is the raw client string. Returns ``True`` when the URL contains\n whitespace, C0 controls or DEL, which would allow header injection when the\n value is later emitted in a ``Location`` header. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n for char in url:\n if char.isspace() or ord(char) < 0x20 or ord(char) == 0x7F:\n return True\n return False\n\n\ndef validate_destination_url(url: str, *, dns_enabled: bool) -> str:\n \"\"\"Validate a caller supplied destination URL before it is stored.\n\n ``url`` is the raw string from the request body and ``dns_enabled`` selects\n whether hostnames are resolved and every resulting address denylist checked.\n Returns the URL unchanged (the exact value that will be stored and later\n served). Raises :class:`app.errors.ApiError` with code ``unsupported_scheme``\n for any scheme other than http/https, ``invalid_url`` for a structurally\n unusable URL or embedded credentials, and ``blocked_destination`` when the\n host is or resolves to a non public address (including unresolvable hosts,\n which fail closed).\n \"\"\"\n if _has_forbidden_characters(url):\n raise ApiError(400, \"invalid_url\", \"The url contains invalid characters.\")\n\n try:\n parts = urlsplit(url)\n except ValueError:\n raise ApiError(400, \"invalid_url\", \"The url could not be parsed.\")\n\n scheme = (parts.scheme or \"\").lower()\n if scheme not in ALLOWED_SCHEMES:\n raise ApiError(\n 400,\n \"unsupported_scheme\",\n \"Only http and https URLs are supported.\",\n )\n\n if parts.username is not None or parts.password is not None:\n raise ApiError(\n 400,\n \"invalid_url\",\n \"Embedded credentials are not allowed in the url.\",\n )\n\n try:\n port = parts.port\n except ValueError:\n raise ApiError(400, \"invalid_url\", \"The url contains an invalid port.\")\n if port is not None and (port < 1 or port > 65535):\n raise ApiError(400, \"invalid_url\", \"The url contains an invalid port.\")\n\n host = parts.hostname\n if not host:\n raise ApiError(400, \"invalid_url\", \"The url must include a host.\")\n if len(host) > MAX_HOST_LENGTH:\n raise ApiError(400, \"invalid_url\", \"The url host is too long.\")\n\n literal = parse_host_as_ip(host)\n if literal is not None:\n if is_blocked_address(literal):\n raise ApiError(400, \"blocked_destination\", BLOCKED_MESSAGE)\n return url\n\n if not dns_enabled:\n return url\n\n addresses = resolve_host(host)\n if not addresses:\n raise ApiError(\n 400,\n \"blocked_destination\",\n \"The destination host could not be resolved.\",\n )\n for text in addresses:\n try:\n resolved = ipaddress.ip_address(text)\n except ValueError:\n # No prose outside it.", "text": "{\"raw_requirement\":\"Add per-API-key rate limiting to the existing URL shortener. Keys come from the environment (SHORTENER_API_KEYS, comma-separated key:quota pairs; quota is requests per minute for link creation). No admin surface, no schema change; an unknown key is treated as no key. Caller presents X-API-Key. Known key -> limited against that key's quota; no key or unknown key -> existing per-IP limit unchanged. Over quota -> HTTP 429 with Retry-After in whole seconds until the window resets. Additive change: the existing per-IP throttle on redirects stays exactly as it is; per-key limiting applies only to link creation and redirects are never limited by key.\",\"intent\":\"Give operators a way to grant named API callers their own link-creation budget: the URL shortener must read a static key-to-quota map from the environment, meter POST /api/links against the quota of the key presented in X-API-Key, and fall back to today's per-IP throttle for anonymous or unrecognised callers, while every existing behaviour (redirect throttling, destination validation, redirect contract, storage layout) stays exactly as it is.\",\"acceptance_criteria\":[\"With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\\\"alpha:100,beta:20\\\" and the limiter enabled, 100 POST /api/links requests carrying `X-API-Key: alpha` inside one 60 second window all return 201; the 101st returns 429 with the envelope {\\\"error\\\":{\\\"code\\\":\\\"rate_limited\\\",...}}, a Retry-After header, and no new row in `links`.\",\"With the same configuration, a caller presenting `X-API-Key: beta` receives 201 for the first 20 creations in the window and 429 for the 21st, proving the quota is read per key and not from LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX.\",\"Two callers presenting different known keys (alpha and beta) from the same client address do not consume each other's budget: after alpha is exhausted, the next beta request still returns 201.\",\"A caller presenting a known key whose quota exceeds LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX (alpha:100 with LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10) receives 201 for the 11th consecutive creation from one address, proving the per-IP creation bucket is not applied to keyed requests.\",\"A POST /api/links request with no X-API-Key header is limited exactly as today: with LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10 the first 10 requests from one client address return 201 and the 11th returns 429 with Retry-After.\",\"A POST /api/links request carrying `X-API-Key: gamma` (not present in SHORTENER_API_KEYS) is metered on the same per-IP bucket as an anonymous request: 10 gamma requests plus 1 anonymous request from the same address produce a 429 on the 11th.\",\"An empty or whitespace-only X-API-Key header value is treated as no key and follows the per-IP path.\",\"When SHORTENER_API_KEYS is unset or empty, every existing rate limit test in tests/test_rate_limit.py still passes unchanged (per-IP limits, LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX honoured, LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false disables limiting, no client address on disk).\",\"The Retry-After value on a key-limited 429 is a decimal string of whole seconds, is >= 1, is <= 60, and int(value) parses without error.\",\"With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false, 15 consecutive POST /api/links with `X-API-Key: beta` (quota 20 exceeded is not the point; the flag is) all return 201, i.e. the key limiter is disabled by the same flag as the IP limiter.\",\"GET /{code} carrying `X-API-Key: alpha` is never metered against alpha's quota: after alpha's creation quota is window.\",\"The existing per-IP redirect throttle is unchanged: with LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10 and the multiplier in app/ratelimit.py, redirect requests from one address are still permitted up to /api/links with a `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:` or `ftp:` url returns 400 with error code `unsupported_scheme` and writes no row, and this holds identically for a request carrying a valid `X-API-Key: alpha` and for an anonymous request.\",\"POST /api/links targeting http://127.0.0.1/x, http://10.0.0.1/x, http://172.16.0.5/x, http://192.168.1.1/x, http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/, http://[::1]/x or a hostname resolving to any of those returns 400 with error code `blocked_destination` and writes no row, unchanged, including when a valid API key is presented.\",\"GET /{code} emits a Location header whose value is byte-for-byte the http(s) URL stored in the `links` row (percent-encoded only when non-ASCII); no request header, query The handler does not SELECT to check availability first; it inserts and lets the database arbitrate, so two concurrent inserts of the same code cannot both succeed."}}, "prompt": "INTENT\nCallers of the URL shortener who present a recognised API key in X-API-Key get their link-creation requests throttled against that key's own per-minute quota instead of the shared per-IP budget, while every other caller and every redirect keeps behaving exactly as it does today.\n\nACCEPTANCE CRITERIA\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100,beta:20\", LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, 100 consecutive POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from one client address all return 201, and the 101st within the same 60-second window returns 429 with body {\"error\":{\"code\":\"rate_limited\",...}} and writes no row to links.\n- With the same configuration, 20 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: beta return 201 and the 21st returns 429; a subsequent POST carrying X-API-Key: alpha in the same window still returns 201, proving key buckets are independent.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100\" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, five POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from a single client address all return 201, proving a known key is not additionally charged against the per-IP creation bucket.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100\" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: gamma (unknown) returns 201 for the first 10 requests from one address and 429 on the 11th; no request returns 401 or 403.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS set, POST /api/links carrying no X-API-Key header behaves byte-for-byte as today: 201 up to LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX per client key, then 429 with Retry-After.\n- A keyed 429 response carries a Retry-After header whose value is a decimal string of whole seconds, is >= 1 and <= 60, contains no fractional part, and is accompanied by Cache-Control: no-store.\n- After the 60-second window for an exhausted key has elapsed (simulated by advancing the limiter clock, not by sleeping), the next POST /api/links with that key returns 201.\n- With alpha's creation quota exhausted, GET /{code} carrying X-API-Key: alpha still returns 307 with the stored Location, and remains limited only by the existing per-IP redirect bucket (LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 per window).\n- GET /api/links/{code}/stats carrying X-API-Key: alpha returns 200 and is never rate limited, before or after the key's creation quota is exhausted.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS unset or empty, every request, including one carrying X-API-Key: alpha, produces exactly the status codes, headers and bodies the service produces today; the entire existing test suite passes unmodified.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha,beta:abc,gamma:0,:5,delta:20\", the application starts, POST /api/links with X-API-Key: delta is limited at 20 per minute, and X-API-Key values alpha, beta, gamma fall back to the per-IP limit; no exception is raised and no malformed value appears in a response body.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\" alpha : 100 , beta:20 \", X-API-Key: alpha is limited at 100 per minute (surrounding whitespace on names and quotas is trimmed).\n- Key matching is exact and case-sensitive: with SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100\" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, the third POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: ALPHA from one address returns 429.\n- With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:1\", 15 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha all return 201.\n- After exercising the key limiter, PRAGMA table_info(links) and PRAGMA table_info(clicks) return exactly the columns they return today, no new table exists in the database, and the raw bytes of every file in the database directory contain neither the string \"alpha\" as a key value nor any client IP address.\n- A 429 caused by the key limiter never echoes the presented X-API-Key value in its body or headers, and no log record emitted at LINKS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG during the request contains the key value.\n\nCONSTRAINTS\n- Python with FastAPI 0.115.6 / Starlette 0.41.3 / pydantic 2.10.4 exactly as pinned in requirements.txt; no new runtime dependency.\n- Environment variable name is exactly SHORTENER_API_KEYS (no LINKS_ prefix) and the request header is exactly X-API-Key (matched case-insensitively per HTTP header rules).\n- No SQLite schema change: no new table, column or index; app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS must remain as-is.\n- No new HTTP endpoint, no admin surface, and no change to the existing routes' contracts other than the added 429 condition on POST /api/links.\n- All existing environment variables keep their current names, defaults, ranges and semantics; the existing tests in tests/ must pass unmodified.\n- The existing per-IP throttle on GET /{code} (bucket 'redirect', REDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER = 100) must remain byte-for-byte equivalent in behaviour; redirects are never limited by API key.\n- Rate limiting continues to run as ASGI middleware ahead of routing and body parsing, so a throttled creation never reaches the database.\n- API key values are credentials: they must never be written to SQLite, the WAL, any file or any log record, and must never appear in a response body or header; limiter state must key on a per-boot salted hash exactly as client addresses do today.\n- Limiter state stays in-process, thread-safe under the existing lock, and bounded in memory; adding key buckets must not let per-IP bucket pruning (MAX_TRACKED_KEYS) regress.\n- Error responses keep the stable envelope {\"error\":{\"code\":...,\"message\":...}}; Every acceptance criterion must be satisfiable by an endpoint you listed, and every endpoint must trace to a criterion.", "skill_id": "design", "system": "You are the API designer for an automated software delivery pipeline. Your output is the contract that implementation, tests and documentation are each generated from independently. Anything you leave vague gets decided three times, differently, and the tests will agree with the code while both disagree with the docs.\n\nDesign the smallest API that satisfies the acceptance criteria. Every endpoint you add is code, tests, docs and attack surface that someone maintains.\n\nFor each endpoint give the method, the path, the request shape with its validation rules, the response shape, and every status code it can return including the failures. If a query on the hot path would scan the table, say so and add the index.\n\nDecisions carry rationale and the alternative you rejected. \"Use SQLite\" is not a decision. \"SQLite in WAL mode, because deployment is single node and the redirect path is a primary key lookup\" is.\n\nTwo decisions are mandatory for a redirect service.\n\nRedirect status code. Choose 302 or 307 and justify it in terms of what the service loses otherwise. A 301 is cached by browsers and intermediaries effectively forever: after a link is found to be malicious it cannot be killed because the client stops asking the service, and every one of those clicks is invisible to analytics. Pick 307 when the request method must survive the redirect, 302 otherwise. Put the choice and the reasoning in redirect_status_code, and do not leave it to the implementer.\n\nShort code generation. Codes are drawn at random from a base62 alphabet, uniqueness is enforced by a UNIQUE constraint in the database rather than by a check before the insert, and a collision retries a small bounded number of times before returning a clean error instead of looping. A hash of the target URL is also rejected, since it leaks whether a given URL was already shortened and makes two users share one code. Implementation and test authoring run at the same time from this design and never see each other's output, so anything both of them touch has to be pinned here or they will each invent a reasonable name and disagree. List every environment variable with its exact name and default. This has already gone wrong once: the service read DATABASE_PATH while the tests set LINKS_DB_PATH, both sensible, and every test that checked persistence failed.\n\nReturn one JSON object matching the schema. This change is additive and confined to the ASGI rate-limiting middleware and the frozen Settings snapshot: when SHORTENER_API_KEYS is configured and the request presents an exactly-matching X-API-Key on POST /api/links, the request is charged against that key's own per-minute bucket instead of the shared per-IP creation bucket. app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS must remain as-is.\n- No new HTTP endpoint, no admin surface, and no change to the existing routes' contracts other than the added 429 condition on POST /api/links.\n- All existing environment variables keep their current names, defaults, ranges and semantics; the entire existing test suite passes unmodified.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha,beta:abc,gamma:0,:5,delta:20\", the application starts, POST /api/links with X-API-Key: delta is limited at 20 per minute, and X-API-Key values alpha, beta, gamma fall back to the per-IP limit; no exception is raised and no malformed value appears in a response body.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\" alpha : 100 , beta:20 \", X-API-Key: alpha is limited at 100 per minute (surrounding whitespace on names and quotas is trimmed).\n- Key matching is exact and case-sensitive: with SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100\" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, the third POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: ALPHA from one address returns 429.\n- With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:1\", 15 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha all return 201.\n- After exercising the key limiter, PRAGMA table_info(links) and PRAGMA table_info(clicks) return exactly the columns they return today, no new table exists in the database, and the raw bytes of every file in the database directory contain neither the string \"alpha\" as a key value nor any client IP address.\n- A 429 caused by the key limiter never echoes the presented X-API-Key value in its body or headers, and no log record emitted at LINKS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG during the request contains the key value.\n\nCONSTRAINTS\n- Python with FastAPI 0.115.6 / Starlette 0.41.3 / pydantic 2.10.4 exactly as pinned in requirements.txt; no new runtime dependency.\n- Environment variable name is exactly SHORTENER_API_KEYS (no LINKS_ prefix) and the request header is exactly X-API-Key (matched case-insensitively per HTTP header rules).\n- No SQLite schema change: no new table, column or index; app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS must remain as-is.\n- No new HTTP endpoint, no admin surface, and no change to the existing routes' contracts other than the added 429 condition on POST /api/links.\n- All existing environment variables keep their current names, defaults, ranges and semantics; redirects are never limited by API key.\n- Rate limiting continues to run as ASGI middleware ahead of routing and body parsing, so a throttled creation never reaches the database.\n- API key values are credentials: they must never be written to SQLite, the WAL, any file or any log record, and must never appear in a response body or header; Every acceptance criterion must be satisfiable by an endpoint you listed, and every endpoint must trace to a criterion.", "skill_id": "design", "system": "You are the API designer for an automated software delivery pipeline. Your output is the contract that implementation, tests and documentation are each generated from independently. Anything you leave vague gets decided three times, differently, and the tests will agree with the code while both disagree with the docs.\n\nDesign the smallest API that satisfies the acceptance criteria. Every endpoint you add is code, tests, docs and attack surface that someone maintains.\n\nFor each endpoint give the method, the path, the request shape with its validation rules, the response shape, and every status code it can return including the failures. If a query on the hot path would scan the table, say so and add the index.\n\nDecisions carry rationale and the alternative you rejected. \"Use SQLite\" is not a decision. \"SQLite in WAL mode, because deployment is single node and the redirect path is a primary key lookup\" is.\n\nTwo decisions are mandatory for a redirect service.\n\nRedirect status code. Choose 302 or 307 and justify it in terms of what the service loses otherwise. A 301 is cached by browsers and intermediaries effectively forever: after a link is found to be malicious it cannot be killed because the client stops asking the service, and every one of those clicks is invisible to analytics. Pick 307 when the request method must survive the redirect, 302 otherwise. Put the choice and the reasoning in redirect_status_code, and do not leave it to the implementer.\n\nShort code generation. Codes are drawn at random from a base62 alphabet, uniqueness is enforced by a UNIQUE constraint in the database rather than by a check before the insert, and a collision retries a small bounded number of times before returning a clean error instead of looping. A hash of the target URL is also rejected, since it leaks whether a given URL was already shortened and makes two users share one code. Implementation and test authoring run at the same time from this design and never see each other's output, so anything both of them touch has to be pinned here or they will each invent a reasonable name and disagree.
