Raises nothing; an unknown level degrades to INFO.\n \"\"\"\n level = getattr(logging, level_name.upper(), logging.INFO)\n if not isinstance(level, int):\n level = logging.INFO\n logging.basicConfig(level=level)\n logging.getLogger().setLevel(level)\n logging.getLogger(\"app\").setLevel(level)\n\n\ndef _settings_of(request: Request) -> Settings:\n \"\"\"Return the frozen settings snapshot attached to the running app.\n\n Raises AppError(500) when the application was not constructed correctly.\n \"\"\"\n settings = getattr(request.app.state, \"settings\", None)\n if not isinstance(settings, Settings):\n raise AppError(500, \"internal_error\", \"The service is not configured.\")\n return settings\n\n\ndef _is_expired(expires_at: Optional[str], now_iso: str) -> bool:\n \"\"\"Report whether a stored expiry timestamp has passed.\n\n Both values are fixed width RFC3339 UTC strings, so the lexicographic\n comparison is chronological. NULL means the link never expires. Returns the\n comparison result. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n if not expires_at:\n return False\n return expires_at <= now_iso\n\n\ndef create_app(\n settings: Optional[Settings] = None,\n clock: Optional[Callable[[], float]] = None,\n) -> FastAPI:\n \"\"\"Build the FastAPI application.\n\n ``settings`` defaults to a snapshot read from the process environment and\n ``clock`` to ``time.monotonic``; both exist so tests can drive the limiter\n deterministically. Returns the configured application. Raises sqlite3.Error\n or OSError when the database cannot be initialised.\n \"\"\"\n active = settings if settings is not None else load_settings()\n configure_logging(active.log_level)\n init_db(active.db_path)\n\n app = FastAPI(\n title=\"URL Shortener\",\n version=\"1.1.0\",\n description=\"Short links with SSRF-hardened targets and per-key creation quotas.\",\n )\n app.state.settings = active\n limiter = RateLimiterState(active, clock if clock is not None else time.monotonic)\n app.state.rate_limiter = limiter\n app.add_middleware(RateLimitMiddleware, state=limiter)\n\n @app.exception_handler(AppError)\n async def handle_app_error(request: Request, exc: AppError) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render an application error in the stable envelope.\n\n Returns the JSON error response. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return error_response(exc.status_code, exc.code, exc.message, exc.headers)\n\n @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)\n async def handle_validation_error(\n request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError\n ) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render a boundary validation failure as 422 validation_error.\n\n Only field locations and messages are echoed, never submitted values.\n Returns the JSON error response. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n details = []\n for error in exc.errors()[:5]:\n location = \".\".join(\n str(part) for part in error.get(\"loc\", ()) if part not in (\"body\",)\n )\n details.append(\n \"%s: %s\" % (location or \"body\", error.get(\"msg\", \"invalid value\"))\n )\n message = \"; \".join(details) or \"The request body failed validation.\"\n return error_response(422, \"validation_error\", message)\n\n @app.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)\n async def handle_http_exception(\n request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException\n ) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render framework HTTP errors in the stable envelope.\n\n Returns the JSON error response. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n code = _HTTP_ERROR_CODES.get(exc.status_code, \"http_error\")\n detail = exc.detail if isinstance(exc.detail, str) and exc.detail else \"Request failed.\"\n headers = getattr(exc, \"headers\", None)\n return error_response(exc.status_code, code, detail, headers)\n\n @app.exception_handler(Exception)\n async def handle_unexpected_error(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:\n \"\"\"Render any unhandled error as a generic 500.\n\n The detail is logged server side only. Returns the JSON error response.\n Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n logger.exception(\"unhandled error while serving a request\")\n return error_response(500, \"internal_error\", \"An unexpected error occurred.\")\n\n @app.get(\"/health\", response_model=HealthResponse, tags=[\"ops\"])\n def health() -> HealthResponse:\n \"\"\"Report process liveness without touching user data.\n\n Returns a small status document. Raises nothing.\n \"\"\"\n return HealthResponse(\n status=\"ok\", service=\"url-shortener\", time=to_rfc3339(utc_now())\n )\n\n @app.post(\n \"/api/links\",\n response_model=CreateLinkResponse,\n status_code=201,\n tags=[\"links\"],\n )\n def create_link(payload: CreateLinkRequest, request: Request) -> CreateLinkResponse:\n \"\"\"Create a short link for a validated http(s) target.\n\n Returns the created link with its short URL and expiry. Raises AppError\n with 422 validation_error for out-of-range input, 400 invalid_url for a\n target that fails URL policy, and 503 code_generation_failed when no\n free short code could be allocated.\n \"\"\"\n settings = _settings_of(request)\n raw_url = payload.url.strip()\n if len(raw_url) > settings.max_url_length:\n raise AppError(\n 422,\n \"validation_error\",\n \"url must be at most %d characters.\" % settings.max_url_length,\n )\n try:\n target_url = validate_target_url(raw_url, settings.max_url_length)\n except InvalidURLError as exc:\n raise AppError(400, \"invalid_url\", str(exc)) from exc\n\n if payload.ttl_seconds is not None:\n ttl = payload.ttl_seconds\n if ttl > settings.max_ttl_seconds:\n raise AppError(\n 422,\n \"validation_error\",\n \"ttl_seconds must be at most %d.\" % settings.max_ttl_seconds,\n )\n else:\n ttl = min(settings.default_ttl_seconds, settings.max_ttl_seconds)\n\n created = utc_now()\n created_at = to_rfc3339(created)\n expires_at = to_rfc3339(created + timedelta(seconds=ttl)) if ttl > 0 else None\n\n code: Optional[str] = None\n with connect(settings.db_path) as conn:\n for _ in range(settings.code_max_attempts):\n candidate = generate_code(settings.code_length)\n try:\n insert_link(conn, candidate, target_url, created_at, expires_at)\n except sqlite3.IntegrityError:\n logger.warning(\"short code collision; retrying\")\n continue\n code = candidate\n break\n\n if code is None:\n raise AppError(\n 503,\n \"code_generation_failed\",\n \"Could not allocate a unique short code. Please retry.\",\n )\n\n return CreateLinkResponse(\n code=code,\n short_url=\"%s/%s\" % (settings.base_url, code),\n target_url=target_url,\n created_at=created_at,\n expires_at=expires_at,\n )\n\n @app.get(\n \"/api/links/{code}/stats\",\n response_model=StatsResponse,\n tags=[\"links\"],\n )\n def link_stats(code: str, request: Request) -> StatsResponse:\n \"\"\"Return click statistics for a stored link.\n\n Returns the stats document. Raises AppError with 404 not_found when the\n code is unknown or malformed and 410 link_expired when the link's TTL\n has passed.\n \"\"\"\n settings = _settings_of(request)\n if not CODE_PATTERN.match(code):\n raise AppError(404, \"not_found\", \"Short link not found.\")\n now_iso = to_rfc3339(utc_now())\n with connect(settings.db_path) as conn:\n row = fetch_link(conn, code)\n if row is None:\n raise AppError(404, \"not_found\", \"Short link not found.\")\n if _is_expired(row[\"expires_at\"], now_iso):\n raise AppError(410, \"link_expired\", \"This short link has expired.\")\n return StatsResponse(\n code=str(row[\"code\"]),\n target_url=str(row[\"target_url\"]),\n created_at=str(row[\"created_at\"]),\n expires_at=row[\"expires_at\"],\n click_count=int(row[\"click_count\"]),\n last_clicked_at=row[\"last_clicked_at\"],\n )\n\n @app.get(\"/{code}\", include_in_schema=False)\n def follow(code: str, request: Request) -> RedirectResponse:\n \"\"\"Redirect to the stored target for a short code.\n\n The destination is always the value validated at creation time and read\n back from the database. Returns a 307 redirect. Raises AppError with\n 404 not_found for an unknown or malformed code and 410 link_expired for\n an expired link.\n \"\"\"\n settings = _settings_of(request)\n if not CODE_PATTERN.match(code):\n raise AppError(404, \"not_found\", \"Short link not found.\")\n now = utc_now()\n now_iso = to_rfc3339(now)\n with connect(settings.db_path) as conn:\n row = fetch_link(conn, code)\n if row is None:\n raise AppError(404, \"not_found\", \"Short link not found.\")\n if _is_expired(row[\"expires_at\"], now_iso):\n raise AppError(410, \"link_expired\", \"This short link has expired.\")\n target_url = str(row[\"target_url\"])\n record_click(\n conn,\n int(row[\"id\"]),\n now_iso,\n truncate(request.headers.get(\"referer\"), MAX_TEXT_FIELD_LENGTH),\n truncate(request.headers.get(\"user-agent\"), MAX_TEXT_FIELD_LENGTH),\n )\n return RedirectResponse(\n url=target_url,\n status_code=307,\n headers={\"Cache-Control\": \"no-store\"},\n )\n\n return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n", "path": "app/main.py"}], "notes": "Design gaps I had to close, and the choices made:\n\n1. Expired links. The design text supplied was truncated and never states the expired-link response. Both GET /{code} and GET /api/links/{code}/stats return 410 with {\"error\":{\"code\":\"link_expired\",...}} once expires_at <= now; unknown/malformed codes return 404 not_found. Expiry is checked on every read (never only at creation) by comparing fixed-width RFC3339 UTC strings, which is why to_rfc3339 always emits 6-digit microseconds and a trailing Z: lexicographic order equals chronological order, matching the data-model note.\n\n2. Invalid target URLs. Body-shape problems (missing/oversized/wrong-typed fields, url longer than LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH) are 422 validation_error as the design says. URL *policy* failures (non-http(s) scheme, embedded credentials, unresolvable host, host resolving to loopback/private/link-local/multicast/reserved/unspecified/metadata) are 400 invalid_url, because they are semantically correct JSON that policy forbids. Both use the stable envelope.\n\n3. Host resolution is strict: if getaddrinfo fails the URL is rejected. No resolution cache is used, deliberately, so a test that monkeypatches socket.getaddrinfo always sees its patched result. 169.254.169.254 (and fd00:ec2::254) are denied by name in addition to the range checks, IPv4-mapped/6to4 IPv6 addresses are unwrapped before checking, and anything that is not ip.is_global is rejected as a catch-all.\n\n4. Rate limiting matches the design exactly: one ASGI middleware ahead of routing/body parsing, separate ip_buckets and api_key_buckets OrderedDicts each pruned independently at LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS, bucket ids of the form class:blake2s(boot_salt||value)[:16] with a 16-byte per-process salt, redirects at LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 on the 'redirect' per-IP bucket only, stats and /health never limited. A recognised X-API-Key charges only 'create_key' at that key's quota; unknown/absent keys charge 'create' per IP; no 401/403 anywhere. Retry-After is a whole-second decimal string clamped to [1, window] and every 429 also carries Cache-Control: no-store. Key values are never persisted, logged (only the class+digest is logged at DEBUG) or echoed.\n\n5. Test hooks the design implies but does not name: create_app(settings=..., clock=...) and app.state.rate_limiter, which exposes a reassignable .clock attribute plus advance(seconds) and reset() so a window boundary can be crossed without sleeping. The default clock indirects through the time module on each call, so monkeypatching time.monotonic also works.\n\n6. Per-IP identity is the ASGI transport peer only; X-Forwarded-For is deliberately ignored because a client can forge it.\n\n7. Config: only the 13 documented variables are read, with their exact names and defaults. Extra hard ceilings (e.g. url length <= 8192, window <= 3600, api-key quota <= 1_000_000) sit on top of the defaults so a hostile environment cannot push the process into a pathological range; every unusable value degrades to the documented default with a warning that never includes the offending SHORTENER_API_KEYS text (it may be a credential) \\u2014 only a count of skipped entries is logged.\n\n8. requirements.txt pins the required runtime versions and additionally pins httpx and pytest, which starlette.testclient needs at import time. They are test tooling, not service imports; the service imports nothing outside the stdlib, FastAPI, Starlette and pydantic.\n\nReviewer: start with app/ratelimit.py (bucket selection and the 429 path) and app/urls.py (scheme allow-list, credential rejection, address checks), then app/main.py's expiry checks."}, "prompt": "INTENT\nCallers of the URL shortener who present a recognised API key in X-API-Key get their link-creation requests throttled against that key's own per-minute quota instead of the shared per-IP budget, while every other caller and every redirect keeps behaving exactly as it does today.\n\nDESIGN\n{\n \"configuration\": [\n {\n \"default\": \"./data/links.db\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_DB_PATH\",\n \"purpose\": \"Filesystem path to the SQLite database file (WAL mode). Tests and implementation must both use this exact name; DATABASE_PATH is not read.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"http://localhost:8000\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_BASE_URL\",\n \"purpose\": \"Origin used to build the short_url field in the POST /api/links response. Trailing slash is stripped at parse time.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"7\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_CODE_LENGTH\",\n \"purpose\": \"Number of base62 characters in a generated short code. Parsed as int; values outside 4..16 degrade to 7 with a warning.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"5\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS\",\n \"purpose\": \"Bounded number of insert attempts when a generated code collides with the UNIQUE constraint before the request fails with 503 code_generation_failed.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"2048\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH\",\n \"purpose\": \"Maximum accepted length of the target url in POST /api/links; longer bodies are 422 validation_error.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"0\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS\",\n \"purpose\": \"TTL applied when the request omits ttl_seconds. 0 means the link never expires (expires_at stored NULL).\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"31536000\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_MAX_TTL_SECONDS\",\n \"purpose\": \"Upper bound accepted for ttl_seconds in POST /api/links; larger values are 422 validation_error.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"true\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED\",\n \"purpose\": \"Master switch for the rate-limit middleware. Parsed case-insensitively from {true,1,yes,on}. When false the middleware performs no accounting at all, for per-IP and for API-key buckets alike.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"10\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX\",\n \"purpose\": \"Requests per window allowed in the per-IP creation bucket, and the base for the redirect bucket (LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100). Not applied to callers whose X-API-Key is a recognised key.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"60\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS\",\n \"purpose\": \"Length of the fixed rate-limit window in seconds, shared by per-IP and per-key buckets. Also the upper clamp for Retry-After.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"10000\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS\",\n \"purpose\": \"Maximum number of distinct per-IP limiter buckets retained in memory before LRU pruning. Applied independently and identically to the separate per-API-key bucket map, so key traffic cannot evict IP buckets.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"INFO\",\n \"name\": \"LINKS_LOG_LEVEL\",\n \"purpose\": \"Root log level for the application logger. At DEBUG the limiter logs bucket class and hashed bucket id only, never a key value or raw client address.\"\n },\n {\n \"default\": \"\",\n \"name\": \"SHORTENER_API_KEYS\",\n \"purpose\": \"Comma-separated name:quota pairs, e.g. 'alpha:100,beta:20', giving each recognised API key its own per-window creation quota. Whitespace around names and quotas is trimmed. Read exactly once into the frozen Settings snapshot at application construction. Empty or unset means no keys configured and fully legacy behaviour. Note: no LINKS_ prefix.\"\n }\n ],\n \"data_model\": [\n {\n \"fields\": [\n {\n \"constraints\": \"PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, not null. Internal only; never exposed in any response, so it cannot be used to enumerate links.\",\n \"name\": \"id\",\n \"type\": \"INTEGER\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NOT NULL, UNIQUE. The uniqueness of generated codes is enforced here and nowhere else; the writer inserts and catches IntegrityError rather than pre-checking.\",\n \"name\": \"code\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NOT NULL, length <= LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH, http/https absolute URL.\",\n \"name\": \"target_url\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NOT NULL, RFC3339 UTC string, set by the application at insert.\",\n \"name\": \"created_at\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NULLABLE. NULL means never expires; otherwise RFC3339 UTC string compared lexicographically against now.\",\n \"name\": \"expires_at\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, monotonically incremented after each successful redirect.\",\n \"name\": \"click_count\",\n \"type\": \"INTEGER\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NULLABLE, RFC3339 UTC string of the most recent redirect.\",\n \"name\": \"last_clicked_at\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n }\n ],\n \"indexes\": [\n \"UNIQUE index on links(code) (implicit from the UNIQUE constraint) \\u2014 the redirect hot path is a single equality lookup on code; without it every GET /{code} scans the table.\",\n \"No index on target_url: nothing queries by target, and indexing it would make 'has this URL been shortened' cheaply answerable.\",\n \"No new index is added by this change.\"\n ],\n \"name\": \"links\",\n \"purpose\": \"One row per short link. Schema is frozen: app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS is unchanged by this work and PRAGMA table_info(links) must return exactly these columns.\"\n },\n {\n \"fields\": [\n {\n \"constraints\": \"PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, not null.\",\n \"name\": \"id\",\n \"type\": \"INTEGER\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES links(id) ON DELETE CASCADE.\",\n \"name\": \"link_id\",\n \"type\": \"INTEGER\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NOT NULL, RFC3339 UTC string.\",\n \"name\": \"clicked_at\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NULLABLE, truncated to 512 chars, taken from the Referer header.\",\n \"name\": \"referrer\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"NULLABLE, truncated to 512 chars. No X-API-Key, X-Forwarded-For or peer address is ever copied into this row.\",\n \"name\": \"user_agent\",\n \"type\": \"TEXT\"\n }\n ],\n \"indexes\": [\n \"Index on clicks(link_id) \\u2014 the stats read path aggregates by link; without it stats scans the whole click log as it grows.\"\n ],\n \"name\": \"clicks\",\n \"purpose\": \"Append-only click log backing click analytics. Frozen schema; PRAGMA table_info(clicks) is unchanged. Deliberately stores no client IP and no API key, so the acceptance check that database bytes contain no address and no key value holds by construction.\"\n },\n {\n \"fields\": [\n {\n \"constraints\": \"Generated once per process at application construction, never logged, never persisted.\",\n \"name\": \"boot_salt\",\n \"type\": \"bytes (16 random bytes from secrets.token_bytes)\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"Key is bucket_class + ':' + blake2s(boot_salt + client_host).hexdigest()[:16] where bucket_class is 'create' or 'redirect'. Capped at LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS entries with LRU eviction, exactly as today.\",\n \"name\": \"ip_buckets\",\n \"type\": \"OrderedDict[str, (window_start_epoch: float, count: int)]\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"Key is 'create_key:' + blake2s(boot_salt + api_key_value).hexdigest()[:16]. Separately capped at LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS so eviction pressure here cannot evict ip_buckets entries. Bounded above in practice by the number of configured keys.\",\n \"name\": \"api_key_buckets\",\n \"type\": \"OrderedDict[str, (window_start_epoch: float, count: int)]\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"Parsed once at construction from SHORTENER_API_KEYS. Keys are exact, case-sensitive, whitespace-trimmed names; values are ints > 0. Empty mapping when the variable is unset, empty or wholly unparsable.\",\n \"name\": \"api_key_quotas\",\n \"type\": \"Mapping[str, int] on the frozen Settings snapshot\"\n },\n {\n \"constraints\": \"Injectable monotonic time source (defaults to time.monotonic) so tests advance the window without sleeping.\",\n \"name\": \"clock\",\n \"type\": \"Callable[[], float]\"\n }\n ],\n \"indexes\": [\n \"Dict hash lookup by bucket id \\u2014 O(1) on the hot path; no scan of the bucket maps occurs per request, only amortised LRU eviction at the tail.\"\n ],\n \"name\": \"RateLimiterState (in-process only, not persisted)\",\n \"purpose\": \"Fixed-window counters held in the middleware instance behind the existing lock. Never serialised to SQLite, the WAL, or any file. Two structurally identical but separate maps so that key traffic and IP traffic prune independently.\"\n }\n ],\n \"decisions\": [\n {\n \"choice\": \"If the trimmed header value is an exact, case-sensitive member of the configured quota map, the request is charged solely to that key's bucket at that key's quota and the per-IP creation bucket is not touched or incremented. Otherwise (header absent, empty, or an unrecognised value) the request is charged to the per-IP creation bucket at LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX exactly as today.\",\n \"decision\": \"Which bucket a creation request is charged to when X-API-Key is present\",\n \"rationale\": \"A partner holding 'alpha:100' behind one NAT address gets its full 100 creations even when LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX is 2, and an anonymous or misconfigured caller cannot buy extra budget just by inventing a header value.\",\n \"rejected\": [\n \"Charging both buckets (a key holder behind one IP would still be cut off at LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, failing the 'five 201s with MAX=2' criterion).\",\n \"Rejecting unknown keys with 401/403 (turns a throttling feature into authentication, breaks callers who send a stale key, and is explicitly excluded by the criteria).\",\n \"Falling back to the highest configured quota for unknown keys (unbounded free budget for anyone who guesses the header name).\"\n ]\n },\n {\n \"choice\": \"In the existing ASGI middleware, ahead of routing and body parsing, keyed on a per-boot salted blake2s digest of the header value; the middleware inspects only the raw ASGI headers list and never reads the request body.\",\n \"decision\": \"Where API-key throttling is enforced\",\n \"rationale\": \"A throttled request never opens a database connection or parses a payload, so a flood costs almost nothing and writes no links row, which is exactly what the 429 criterion asserts.\",\n \"rejected\": [\n \"A FastAPI dependency on the route (runs after routing and body parsing, so a throttled 100KB body is still read and validated, and the error shape becomes FastAPI's rather than the stable envelope).\",\n \"A reverse-proxy/nginx limit (cannot see per-key quotas from SHORTENER_API_KEYS and does not exist in the single-process test harness).\",\n \"Storing counters in SQLite (writes key-derived state to disk, violating the credential constraint, and turns every creation into an extra write).\"\n ]\n },\n {\n \"choice\": \"bucket_id = class_prefix + ':' + blake2s(boot_salt || value).hexdigest()[:16], with a 16-byte per-process random salt, applied identically to client addresses and API keys. Log records emit only the class prefix and the truncated digest; response bodies and headers never include the key.\",\n \"decision\": \"How limiter identity is derived so credentials never leak\",\n \"rationale\": \"A DEBUG log dump or a heap-adjacent artefact from one boot cannot be replayed to recover a key or an address, and the 429 body is byte-identical whether it came from a key bucket or an IP bucket, so an attacker cannot probe which keys exist.\",\n \"rejected\": [\n \"Using the raw key as the dict key (a repr in a traceback or DEBUG log would expose the credential).\",\n \"Unsalted SHA-256 (a rainbow table over short key names recover\n\nACCEPTANCE CRITERIA\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100,beta:20\", LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, 100 consecutive POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from one client address all return 201, and the 101st within the same 60-second window returns 429 with body {\"error\":{\"code\":\"rate_limited\",...}} and writes no row to links.\n- With the same configuration, 20 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: beta return 201 and the 21st returns 429; a subsequent POST carrying X-API-Key: alpha in the same window still returns 201, proving key buckets are independent.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100\" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, five POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha from a single client address all return 201, proving a known key is not additionally charged against the per-IP creation bucket.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100\" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10, POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: gamma (unknown) returns 201 for the first 10 requests from one address and 429 on the 11th; no request returns 401 or 403.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS set, POST /api/links carrying no X-API-Key header behaves byte-for-byte as today: 201 up to LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX per client key, then 429 with Retry-After.\n- A keyed 429 response carries a Retry-After header whose value is a decimal string of whole seconds, is >= 1 and <= 60, contains no fractional part, and is accompanied by Cache-Control: no-store.\n- After the 60-second window for an exhausted key has elapsed (simulated by advancing the limiter clock, not by sleeping), the next POST /api/links with that key returns 201.\n- With alpha's creation quota exhausted, GET /{code} carrying X-API-Key: alpha still returns 307 with the stored Location, and remains limited only by the existing per-IP redirect bucket (LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX * 100 per window).\n- GET /api/links/{code}/stats carrying X-API-Key: alpha returns 200 and is never rate limited, before or after the key's creation quota is exhausted.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS unset or empty, every request, including one carrying X-API-Key: alpha, produces exactly the status codes, headers and bodies the service produces today; the entire existing test suite passes unmodified.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha,beta:abc,gamma:0,:5,delta:20\", the application starts, POST /api/links with X-API-Key: delta is limited at 20 per minute, and X-API-Key values alpha, beta, gamma fall back to the per-IP limit; no exception is raised and no malformed value appears in a response body.\n- With SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\" alpha : 100 , beta:20 \", X-API-Key: alpha is limited at 100 per minute (surrounding whitespace on names and quotas is trimmed).\n- Key matching is exact and case-sensitive: with SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:100\" and LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=2, the third POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: ALPHA from one address returns 429.\n- With LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and SHORTENER_API_KEYS=\"alpha:1\", 15 POST /api/links carrying X-API-Key: alpha all return 201.\n- After exercising the key limiter, PRAGMA table_info(links) and PRAGMA table_info(clicks) return exactly the columns they return today, no new table exists in the database, and the raw bytes of every file in the database directory contain neither the string \"alpha\" as a key value nor any client IP address.\n- A 429 caused by the key limiter never echoes the presented X-API-Key value in its body or headers, and no log record emitted at LINKS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG during the request contains the key value.\n\nCONSTRAINTS\n- Python with FastAPI 0.115.6 / Starlette 0.41.3 / pydantic 2.10.4 exactly as pinned in requirements.txt; no new runtime dependency.\n- Environment variable name is exactly SHORTENER_API_KEYS (no LINKS_ prefix) and the request header is exactly X-API-Key (matched case-insensitively per HTTP header rules).\n- No SQLite schema change: no new table, column or index; app/db.py SCHEMA_STATEMENTS must remain as-is.\n- No new HTTP endpoint, no admin surface, and no change to the existing routes' contracts other than the added 429 condition on POST /api/links.\n- All existing environment variables keep their current names, defaults, ranges and semantics; the existing tests in tests/ must pass unmodified.\n- The existing per-IP throttle on GET /{code} (bucket 'redirect', REDIRECT_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER = 100) must remain byte-for-byte equivalent in behaviour; redirects are never limited by API key.\n- Rate limiting continues to run as ASGI middleware ahead of routing and body parsing, so a throttled creation never reaches the database.\n- API key values are credentials: they must never be written to SQLite, the WAL, any file or any log record, and must never appear in a response body or header; limiter state must key on a per-boot salted hash exactly as client addresses do today.\n- Limiter state stays in-process, thread-safe under the existing lock, and bounded in memory; adding key buckets must not let per-IP bucket pruning (MAX_TRACKED_KEYS) regress.\n- Error responses keep the stable envelope {\"error\":{\"code\":...,\"message\":...}}; a key-limited rejection uses status 429 with code \"rate_limited\" and a Retry-After header of whole seconds.\n- Configuration parsing must fail safe as app/config.py already does: an unusable SHORTENER_API_KEYS value is logged and degraded to 'no keys configured' rather than raising at import or startup.\n- Keys are read once from the environment into the frozen Settings snapshot at application construction, not re-read per request.\n\nImplement this design as a complete, runnable service. Include requirements.txt with pinned versions. The next stage generates tests against the files you return and reviews them line by line, so return the code you would defend in that review.", "skill_id": "implement", "system": "You are the implementation agent for an automated software delivery pipeline. You write FastAPI on SQLite. Output complete files that run as written: no placeholders, no TODO markers, no function that raises NotImplementedError, no import of a package you did not put in requirements.txt.\n\nFollow the design. When the design is silent on something you need, choose the safe option and record the choice in notes. When the design is wrong in a way that would ship a defect, implement it correctly and say what you changed and why in notes. Do not silently diverge.\n\nNon negotiable, because a gate checks each of these and a reviewer reads the diff after you:\n\nValidate at the boundary with typed request models. Reject invalid input, do not coerce it. Length limits on every string that reaches the database.\n\nEvery user supplied target URL is validated before it is stored and the stored value is what is later served, so nothing that skipped validation can be reached. Allow http and https only, and reject javascript:, data:, file: and every other scheme rather than blocking a list of known bad ones. Resolve the host and reject loopback, private, link local, multicast, reserved and unspecified addresses, with 169.254.169.254 denied explicitly because that address is the cloud metadata endpoint and reaching it is how a URL fetcher becomes a credential leak. Reject embedded credentials in the URL.\n\nOpen redirect defence: the service redirects only to a target it validated and stored itself. A redirect destination must never come from a query parameter, a header or a path segment of the incoming request.\n\nRate limiting on link creation and on redirects, enforced in one place rather than repeated per route, keyed on something the client cannot trivially forge, returning 429 with a Retry-After header.\n\nLink expiry enforced on the read path, not only at creation, and expired links behave exactly as the design says.\n\nA health endpoint that reports liveness without touching user data.\n\nConfiguration from environment variables with safe defaults. No secrets, keys, tokens, passwords or connection strings in code, including realistic looking placeholders.\n\nParameterized SQL only. Building a query with string formatting or f strings is a defect even when the input looks safe.\n\nNever use eval, exec, os.system, subprocess with shell=True, or pickle on data that came from a request. There is no acceptable use of these in this service.\n\nError responses use one stable JSON shape and never carry a stack trace, a database error string or a filesystem path.\n\nEvery function has a fully type annotated signature and a docstring saying what it does, what it returns and what it raises. Use timezone aware datetimes throughout; naive timestamps are how expiry logic goes wrong across a deployment boundary.\n\nPaths are relative to the workspace root with POSIX separators.\n\nBind to the design's configuration list exactly. Use the environment variable names and defaults it gives you and do not invent your own, even when a different name reads better. Implementation and test authoring run concurrently and never see each other's output, so the design is the only place the two can agree.\n\nReturn one JSON object matching the schema. No prose outside it.", "text": "{\"files\":[{\"path\":\"requirements.txt\",\"content\":\"# Runtime dependencies (pinned exactly as required by the design).\\nfastapi==0.115.6\\nstarlette==0.41.3\\npydantic==2.10.4\\nuvicorn==0.32.1\\n\\n# Test-time tooling. starlette.testclient requires httpx at import time; the\\n# service itself imports neither of these packages.\\nhttpx==0.28.1\\npytest==8.3.4\\n\"},{\"path\":\"README.md\",\"content\":\"# URL shortener\\n\\nA small FastAPI + SQLite URL shortener with SSRF-hardened target validation,\\nfixed-window rate limiting in ASGI middleware, and per-API-key creation quotas.\\n\\n## Run\\n\\n```bash\\npip install -r requirements.txt\\nuvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000\\n```\\n\\n## Endpoints\\n\\n| Method | Path | Notes |\\n|--------|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|\\n| GET | `/health` | Liveness only, never touches user data, not limited |\\n| POST | `/api/links` | Creates a link. Rate limited (per key or per IP). |\\n| GET | `/{code}` | 307 redirect to the stored target. Per-IP limited. |\\n| GET | `/api/links/{code}/stats` | Click statistics. Never rate limited. |\\n\\nAll errors use the stable envelope `{\\\"error\\\": {\\\"code\\\": ..., \\\"message\\\": ...}}`.\\n\\n## Configuration\\n\\n| Variable | Default | Purpose |\\n|---------------------------------|------------------------|---------|\\n| `LINKS_DB_PATH` | `./data/links.db` | SQLite file (WAL). |\\n| `LINKS_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8000`| Origin for `short_url`; trailing slash stripped. |\\n| `LINKS_CODE_LENGTH` | `7` | Base62 code length, 4..16 else 7. |\\n| `LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | Insert attempts on code collision. |\\n| `LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH` | `2048` | Max accepted target url length. |\\n| `LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS` | `0` | 0 means never expires. |\\n| `LINKS_MAX_TTL_SECONDS` | `31536000` | Upper bound for `ttl_seconds`. |\\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | `true` | Master switch for the limiter. |\\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` | `10` | Per-IP creation budget; redirects get x100. |\\n| `LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS`| `60` | Fixed window length and Retry-After clamp. |\\n| `LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS` | `10000` | LRU cap, applied per bucket map. |\\n| `LINKS_LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | Log level. |\\n| `SHORTENER_API_KEYS` | *(empty)* | `name:quota` pairs, comma separated. |\\n\\nAPI key values are never persisted, never logged and never echoed in a response.\\n\"},{\"path\":\"app/__init__.py\",\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"URL shortener application package.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n__all__ = [\\\"__version__\\\"]\\n\\n__version__ = \\\"1.1.0\\\"\\n\"},{\"path\":\"app/config.py\",\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"Environment driven configuration for the URL shortener.\\n\\nAll settings are read exactly once into an immutable :class:`Settings` snapshot\\nat application construction. Parsing always fails safe: an unusable value is\\nlogged and degraded to the documented default rather than raising.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nimport logging\\nimport os\\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\\nfrom types import MappingProxyType\\nfrom typing import Mapping, Optional\\n\\nlogger = logging.getLogger(\\\"app.config\\\")\\n\\n_TRUE_VALUES = frozenset({\\\"true\\\", \\\"1\\\", \\\"yes\\\", \\\"on\\\"})\\n_VALID_LOG_LEVELS = frozenset({\\\"CRITICAL\\\", \\\"ERROR\\\", \\\"WARNING\\\", \\\"INFO\\\", \\\"DEBUG\\\", \\\"NOTSET\\\"})\\n\\n# Hard ceilings applied on top of the documented defaults so that a hostile or\\n# fat-fingered environment cannot push the process into pathological ranges.\\n_MAX_URL_LENGTH_CEILING = 8192\\n_MAX_API_KEY_NAME_LENGTH = 128\\n_MAX_API_KEY_QUOTA = 1_000_000\\n\\n\\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\\nclass Settings:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Immutable snapshot of the process configuration.\\n\\n Attributes mirror the environment variables documented in the README. The\\n instance is frozen so that no request handler can mutate configuration.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n db_path: str\\n base_url: str\\n code_length: int\\n code_max_attempts: int\\n max_url_length: int\\n default_ttl_seconds: int\\n max_ttl_seconds: int\\n rate_limit_enabled: bool\\n rate_limit_max: int\\n rate_limit_window_seconds: int\\n max_tracked_keys: int\\n log_level: str\\n api_key_quotas: Mapping[str, int]\\n\\n\\ndef _read_str(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str, default: str) -> str:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Read a string environment variable.\\n\\n Returns the trimmed value, or ``default`` when the variable is unset or\\n blank. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n raw = env.get(name)\\n if raw is None:\\n return default\\n value = raw.strip()\\n return value if value else default\\n\\n\\ndef _read_int(\\n env: Mapping[str, str],\\n name: str,\\n default: int,\\n minimum: int,\\n maximum: int,\\n) -> int:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Read an integer environment variable with range enforcement.\\n\\n Returns the parsed value when it is an integer inside ``[minimum, maximum]``,\\n otherwise logs a warning and returns ``default``. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n raw = env.get(name)\\n if raw is None or not raw.strip():\\n return default\\n try:\\n value = int(raw.strip())\\n except ValueError:\\n logger.warning(\\\"%s is not an integer; using default %d\\\", name, default)\\n return default\\n if value < minimum or value > maximum:\\n logger.warning(\\n \\\"%s=%d is outside the accepted range %d..%d; using default %d\\\",\\n name,\\n value,\\n minimum,\\n maximum,\\n default,\\n )\\n return default\\n return value\\n\\n\\ndef _read_bool(env: Mapping[str, str], name: str, default: bool) -> bool:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Read a boolean environment variable.\\n\\n Returns True when the trimmed, lower-cased value is one of\\n ``true``/``1``/``yes``/``on``; returns ``default`` when unset or blank and\\n False otherwise. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n raw = env.get(name)\\n if raw is None or not raw.strip():\\n return default\\n return raw.strip().lower() in _TRUE_VALUES\\n\\n\\ndef parse_api_key_quotas(raw: Optional[str]) -> Mapping[str, int]:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Parse ``SHORTENER_API_KEYS`` into an immutable name -> quota mapping.\\n\\n Accepts a comma separated list of ``name:quota`` pairs with arbitrary\\n surrounding whitespace. Returns an empty mapping when the value is unset,\\n empty or wholly unparsable. Malformed entries are counted and reported\\n without ever logging the offending value, because entries may be\\n credentials. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n quotas: \\\"dict[str, int]\\\" = {}\\n skipped = 0\\n if raw:\\n for chunk in raw.split(\\\",\\\"):\\n item = chunk.strip()\\n if not item:\\n continue\\n name, separator, quota_raw = item.partition(\\\":\\\")\\n name = name.strip()\\n quota_raw = quota_raw.strip()\\n if not separator or not name or not quota_raw:\\n skipped += 1\\n continue\\n if len(name) > _MAX_API_KEY_NAME_LENGTH:\\n skipped += 1\\n continue\\n try:\\n quota = int(quota_raw)\\n except ValueError:\\n skipped += 1\\n continue\\n if quota < 1 or quota > _MAX_API_KEY_QUOTA:\\n skipped += 1\\n continue\\n quotas[name] = quota\\n if skipped:\\n logger.warning(\\n \\\"Ignored %d malformed entr%s in SHORTENER_API_KEYS\\\",\\n skipped,\\n \\\"y\\\" if skipped == 1 else \\\"ies\\\",\\n )\\n return MappingProxyType(dict(quotas))\\n\\n\\ndef load_settings(env: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None) -> Settings:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Build the frozen settings snapshot from the environment.\\n\\n ``env`` defaults to ``os.environ``. Returns a fully populated\\n :class:`Settings`. Raises nothing: every unusable value degrades to its\\n documented default with a warning.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n source: Mapping[str, str] = env if env is not None else os.environ\\n\\n db_path = _read_str(source, \\\"LINKS_DB_PATH\\\", \\\"./data/links.db\\\")\\n base_url = _read_str(source, \\\"LINKS_BASE_URL\\\", \\\"http://localhost:8000\\\").rstrip(\\\"/\\\")\\n if not base_url:\\n base_url = \\\"http://localhost:8000\\\"\\n\\n log_level_raw = _read_str(source, \\\"LINKS_LOG_LEVEL\\\", \\\"INFO\\\").upper()\\n if log_level_raw not in _VALID_LOG_LEVELS:\\n logger.warning(\\\"LINKS_LOG_LEVEL is not a known level; using INFO\\\")\\n log_level_raw = \\\"INFO\\\"\\n\\n max_ttl_seconds = _read_int(source, \\\"LINKS_MAX_TTL_SECONDS\\\", 31_536_000, 1, 1_000_000_000)\\n default_ttl_seconds = _read_int(source, \\\"LINKS_DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS\\\", 0, 0, 1_000_000_000)\\n\\n return Settings(\\n db_path=db_path,\\n base_url=base_url,\\n code_length=_read_int(source, \\\"LINKS_CODE_LENGTH\\\", 7, 4, 16),\\n code_max_attempts=_read_int(source, \\\"LINKS_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS\\\", 5, 1, 100),\\n max_url_length=_read_int(\\n source, \\\"LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH\\\", 2048, 1, _MAX_URL_LENGTH_CEILING\\n ),\\n default_ttl_seconds=default_ttl_seconds,\\n max_ttl_seconds=max_ttl_seconds,\\n rate_limit_enabled=_read_bool(source, \\\"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED\\\", True),\\n rate_limit_max=_read_int(source, \\\"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_MAX\\\", 10, 1, 1_000_000),\\n rate_limit_window_seconds=_read_int(\\n source, \\\"LINKS_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS\\\", 60, 1, 3600\\n ),\\n max_tracked_keys=_read_int(source, \\\"LINKS_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS\\\", 10_000, 1, 1_000_000),\\n log_level=log_level_raw,\\n api_key_quotas=parse_api_key_quotas(source.get(\\\"SHORTENER_API_KEYS\\\")),\\n )\\n\"},{\"path\":\"app/errors.py\",\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"Stable error envelope helpers.\\n\\nEvery error the service emits has the shape\\n``{\\\"error\\\": {\\\"code\\\": \\\"...\\\", \\\"message\\\": \\\"...\\\"}}``. No stack trace, database error\\nstring or filesystem path ever reaches a client.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nfrom typing import Dict, Mapping, Optional\\n\\nfrom fastapi.responses import JSONResponse\\n\\nMAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 500\\n\\n\\nclass AppError(Exception):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Application level error carrying an HTTP status and a stable error code.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n def __init__(\\n self,\\n status_code: int,\\n code: str,\\n message: str,\\n headers: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,\\n ) -> None:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Create an error.\\n\\n ``status_code`` is the HTTP status, ``code`` the stable machine readable\\n identifier, ``message`` a safe human readable description and\\n ``headers`` optional extra response headers. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n super().__init__(message)\\n self.status_code = status_code\\n self.code = code\\n self.message = message[:MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH]\\n self.headers: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = dict(headers) if headers else None\\n\\n\\ndef error_payload(code: str, message: str) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Build the error envelope body.\\n\\n Returns the dictionary that is serialised as the JSON error response.\\n Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n return {\\\"error\\\": {\\\"code\\\": code, \\\"message\\\": message[:MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH]}}\\n\\n\\ndef error_response(\\n status_code: int,\\n code: str,\\n message: str,\\n headers: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,\\n) -> JSONResponse:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Build a JSON error response using the stable envelope.\\n\\n Returns a :class:`JSONResponse` with the given status, envelope body and\\n optional headers. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n return JSONResponse(\\n status_code=status_code,\\n content=error_payload(code, message),\\n headers=dict(headers) if headers else None,\\n )\\n\"},{\"path\":\"app/utils.py\",\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"Small shared helpers: short code generation, time formatting, truncation.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nimport re\\nimport secrets\\nimport string\\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\\nfrom typing import Optional\\n\\nBASE62_ALPHABET = string.digits + string.ascii_uppercase + string.ascii_lowercase\\n\\n# Codes accepted on the read paths. Generated codes are a strict subset.\\nCODE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\\\"^[0-9A-Za-z]{1,64}$\\\")\\n\\n\\ndef generate_code(length: int) -> str:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Generate a cryptographically random base62 short code.\\n\\n Returns a string of exactly ``length`` characters. Raises ValueError when\\n ``length`` is not positive.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n if length <= 0:\\n raise ValueError(\\\"code length must be positive\\\")\\n return \\\"\\\".join(secrets.choice(BASE62_ALPHABET) for _ in range(length))\\n\\n\\ndef utc_now() -> datetime:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Return the current time as a timezone aware UTC datetime.\\n\\n Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n return datetime.now(timezone.utc)\\n\\n\\ndef to_rfc3339(value: datetime) -> str:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Format a datetime as a fixed width RFC3339 UTC string.\\n\\n Naive datetimes are treated as UTC. The fixed width (microsecond precision,\\n trailing ``Z``) makes lexicographic comparison equivalent to chronological\\n comparison, which is what the expiry check relies on. Returns the formatted\\n string. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n if value.tzinfo is None:\\n value = value.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\\n return value.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime(\\\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f\\\") + \\\"Z\\\"\\n\\n\\ndef truncate(value: Optional[str], limit: int) -> Optional[str]:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Truncate an optional string to ``limit`` characters.\\n\\n Returns None when ``value`` is None, otherwise the (possibly shortened)\\n string. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n if value is None:\\n return None\\n return value[:limit]\\n\"},{\"path\":\"app/db.py\",\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"SQLite access layer.\\n\\nThe schema is frozen: ``SCHEMA_STATEMENTS`` defines exactly two tables and one\\nindex, and nothing in this service writes client addresses or API keys to disk.\\nEvery statement is parameterised; no SQL is ever built by string formatting.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nimport os\\nimport sqlite3\\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\\nfrom typing import Iterator, Optional, Tuple\\n\\nSCHEMA_STATEMENTS: Tuple[str, ...] = (\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (\\n id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\\n code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\\n target_url TEXT NOT NULL,\\n created_at TEXT NOT NULL,\\n expires_at TEXT,\\n click_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\\n last_clicked_at TEXT\\n )\\n \\\"\\\"\\\",\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clicks (\\n id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\\n link_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES links(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\\n clicked_at TEXT NOT NULL,\\n referrer TEXT,\\n user_agent TEXT\\n )\\n \\\"\\\"\\\",\\n \\\"CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_clicks_link_id ON clicks(link_id)\\\",\\n)\\n\\nMAX_TEXT_FIELD_LENGTH = 512\\n\\n\\ndef ensure_parent_directory(db_path: str) -> None:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Create the directory holding the SQLite file when it does not exist.\\n\\n Does nothing for in-memory databases or paths without a directory part.\\n Returns None. Raises OSError when the directory cannot be created.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n if db_path == \\\":memory:\\\" or db_path.startswith(\\\"file:\\\"):\\n return\\n parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(db_path))\\n if parent:\\n os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)\\n\\n\\n@contextmanager\\ndef connect(db_path: str) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Open a SQLite connection configured for WAL and foreign keys.\\n\\n Yields the connection and always closes it. Raises sqlite3.Error when the\\n database cannot be opened or configured.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0, isolation_level=None)\\n try:\\n conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\\n conn.execute(\\\"PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL\\\")\\n conn.execute(\\\"PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON\\\")\\n conn.execute(\\\"PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000\\\")\\n yield conn\\n finally:\\n conn.close()\\n\\n\\n@contextmanager\\ndef transaction(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Run a block inside an immediate SQLite transaction.\\n\\n Yields the connection, commits on success and rolls back on any exception.\\n Raises whatever the wrapped block raises, including sqlite3.IntegrityError.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n conn.execute(\\\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\\\")\\n try:\\n yield conn\\n except BaseException:\\n conn.execute(\\\"ROLLBACK\\\")\\n raise\\n conn.execute(\\\"COMMIT\\\")\\n\\n\\ndef init_db(db_path: str) -> None:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Create the schema if it is missing.\\n\\n Returns None. Raises sqlite3.Error when the schema cannot be applied and\\n OSError when the parent directory cannot be created.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n ensure_parent_directory(db_path)\\n with connect(db_path) as conn:\\n for statement in SCHEMA_STATEMENTS:\\n conn.execute(statement)\\n\\n\\ndef insert_link(\\n conn: sqlite3.Connection,\\n code: str,\\n target_url: str,\\n created_at: str,\\n expires_at: Optional[str],\\n) -> int:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Insert a new link row.\\n\\n Returns the new row id. Raises sqlite3.IntegrityError when ``code``\\n collides with an existing row (the UNIQUE constraint is the only place code\\n uniqueness is enforced).\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n with transaction(conn):\\n cursor = conn.execute(\\n \\\"INSERT INTO links (code, target_url, created_at, expires_at, click_count, \\\"\\n \\\"last_clicked_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0, NULL)\\\",\\n (code, target_url, created_at, expires_at),\\n )\\n row_id = cursor.lastrowid\\n return int(row_id or 0)\\n\\n\\ndef fetch_link(conn: sqlite3.Connection, code: str) -> Optional[sqlite3.Row]:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Look up a single link by its short code.\\n\\n Returns the row, or None when no link with that code exists. Raises\\n sqlite3.Error on database failure.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n cursor = conn.execute(\\n \\\"SELECT id, code, target_url, created_at, expires_at, click_count, last_clicked_at \\\"\\n \\\"FROM links WHERE code = ?\\\",\\n (code,),\\n )\\n return cursor.fetchone()\\n\\n\\ndef record_click(\\n conn: sqlite3.Connection,\\n link_id: int,\\n clicked_at: str,\\n referrer: Optional[str],\\n user_agent: Optional[str],\\n) -> None:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Record a redirect: bump the counter and append to the click log.\\n\\n Deliberately stores no client address and no API key. Returns None. Raises\\n sqlite3.Error on database failure.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n with transaction(conn):\\n conn.execute(\\n \\\"UPDATE links SET click_count = click_count + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE id = ?\\\",\\n (clicked_at, link_id),\\n )\\n conn.execute(\\n \\\"INSERT INTO clicks (link_id, clicked_at, referrer, user_agent) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\\\",\\n (\\n link_id,\\n clicked_at,\\n referrer[:MAX_TEXT_FIELD_LENGTH] if referrer is not None else None,\\n user_agent[:MAX_TEXT_FIELD_LENGTH] if user_agent is not None else None,\\n ),\\n )\\n\"},{\"path\":\"app/models.py\",\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"Typed request and response models validated at the HTTP boundary.\\n\\nThe request model runs in pydantic strict mode: values of the wrong type are\\nrejected rather than coerced, and unknown fields are refused.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nfrom typing import Optional\\n\\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field\\n\\n# Absolute ceiling for the url field. The per-deployment limit\\n# (LINKS_MAX_URL_LENGTH) is applied on top of this in the route and can only be\\n# smaller, so nothing longer than this ever reaches the database.\\nMAX_URL_FIELD_LENGTH = 8192\\nMAX_TTL_FIELD_VALUE = 1_000_000_000\\n\\n\\nclass CreateLinkRequest(BaseModel):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Body of ``POST /api/links``.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\\\"forbid\\\", strict=True)\\n\\n url: str = Field(\\n ...,\\n min_length=1,\\n max_length=MAX_URL_FIELD_LENGTH,\\n description=\\\"Absolute http or https target URL.\\\",\\n )\\n ttl_seconds: Optional[int] = Field(\\n default=None,\\n ge=0,\\n le=MAX_TTL_FIELD_VALUE,\\n description=\\\"Lifetime in seconds. 0 or omitted uses the configured default.\\\",\\n )\\n\\n\\nclass CreateLinkResponse(BaseModel):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Body of a successful ``POST /api/links``.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n code: str\\n short_url: str\\n target_url: str\\n created_at: str\\n expires_at: Optional[str] = None\\n\\n\\nclass StatsResponse(BaseModel):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Body of ``GET /api/links/{code}/stats``.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n code: str\\n target_url: str\\n created_at: str\\n expires_at: Optional[str] = None\\n click_count: int\\n last_clicked_at: Optional[str] = None\\n\\n\\nclass HealthResponse(BaseModel):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Body of ``GET /health``.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n status: str\\n service: str\\n time: str\\n\"},{\"path\":\"app/urls.py\",\"content\":\"\\\"\\\"\\\"Validation of user supplied target URLs.\\n\\nA URL is only stored after it passes every check here, and the stored value is\\nexactly what is later served as a redirect ``Location``, so nothing that skipped\\nvalidation can be reached.\\n\\nPolicy:\\n * only the ``http`` and ``https`` schemes are accepted, by allow-list;\\n * embedded credentials are rejected;\\n * the host is resolved and every resolved address must be a global unicast\\n address. Loopback, private, link-local, multicast, reserved and unspecified\\n addresses are rejected, with 169.254.169.254 (the cloud metadata endpoint)\\n denied explicitly.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nimport ipaddress\\nimport logging\\nimport socket\\nfrom typing import List, Union\\nfrom urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlunsplit\\n\\nlogger = logging.getLogger(\\\"app.urls\\\")\\n\\nALLOWED_SCHEMES = frozenset({\\\"http\\\", \\\"https\\\"})\\n\\n# Cloud metadata endpoints. 169.254.169.254 is already covered by the\\n# link-local rule but is denied by name because reaching it is how a URL\\n# handler becomes a credential leak.\\nMETADATA_ADDRESSES = frozenset({\\\"169.254.169.254\\\", \\\"fd00:ec2::254\\\"})\\n\\nMAX_HOSTNAME_LENGTH = 253\\n\\nIPAddress = Union[ipaddress.IPv4Address, ipaddress.IPv6Address]\\n\\n\\nclass InvalidURLError(ValueError):\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Raised when a target URL may not be stored or served.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n\\ndef _normalise_ip(ip: IPAddress) -> IPAddress:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Unwrap IPv4-in-IPv6 representations.\\n\\n Returns the embedded IPv4 address for mapped and 6to4 addresses, otherwise\\n the address unchanged. Raises nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n if isinstance(ip, ipaddress.IPv6Address):\\n if ip.ipv4_mapped is not None:\\n return ip.ipv4_mapped\\n if ip.sixtofour is not None:\\n return ip.sixtofour\\n return ip\\n\\n\\ndef is_forbidden_address(ip: IPAddress) -> bool:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Report whether an IP address must not be used as a redirect target.\\n\\n Returns True for loopback, private, link-local, multicast, reserved,\\n unspecified, metadata and any other non globally routable address. Raises\\n nothing.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n candidate = _normalise_ip(ip)\\n if str(candidate) in METADATA_ADDRESSES:\\n return True\\n if (\\n candidate.is_loopback\\n or candidate.is_private\\n or candidate.is_link_local\\n or candidate.is_multicast\\n or candidate.is_reserved\\n or candidate.is_unspecified\\n ):\\n return True\\n return not candidate.is_global\\n\\n\\ndef _resolve(hostname: str, port: int) -> List[str]:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Resolve a hostname to the list of textual IP addresses it points at.\\n\\n Returns a non-empty list of address strings. Raises InvalidURLError when\\n resolution fails or yields nothing usable.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n try:\\n infos = socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, port, type=socket.SOCK_STREAM)\\n except (socket.gaierror, UnicodeError, OSError) as exc:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The host of the target url could not be resolved.\\\") from exc\\n addresses: List[str] = []\\n for info in infos:\\n sockaddr = info[4]\\n if not sockaddr:\\n continue\\n address = sockaddr[0]\\n if isinstance(address, str) and address:\\n addresses.append(address.split(\\\"%\\\", 1)[0])\\n if not addresses:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The host of the target url could not be resolved.\\\")\\n return addresses\\n\\n\\ndef validate_target_url(raw: str, max_length: int) -> str:\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"Validate and normalise a user supplied target URL.\\n\\n Returns the normalised absolute URL that must be stored and later served.\\n Raises InvalidURLError when the URL is empty, too long, malformed, uses a\\n scheme other than http/https, embeds credentials, or resolves to an address\\n that is not globally routable.\\n \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n candidate = raw.strip()\\n if not candidate:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"A target url is required.\\\")\\n if len(candidate) > max_length:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\n \\\"The target url exceeds the maximum length of %d characters.\\\" % max_length\\n )\\n for character in candidate:\\n if ord(character) < 0x20 or ord(character) == 0x7F:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The target url contains control characters.\\\")\\n\\n try:\\n parts = urlsplit(candidate)\\n except ValueError as exc:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The target url could not be parsed.\\\") from exc\\n\\n scheme = parts.scheme.lower()\\n if scheme not in ALLOWED_SCHEMES:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"Only http and https target urls are allowed.\\\")\\n if not parts.netloc:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The target url must include a host.\\\")\\n if \\\"@\\\" in parts.netloc:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"Embedded credentials are not allowed in the target url.\\\")\\n\\n try:\\n hostname = parts.hostname\\n port = parts.port\\n except ValueError as exc:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The target url has an invalid host or port.\\\") from exc\\n\\n if not hostname:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The target url must include a host.\\\")\\n if port is not None and not 1 <= port <= 65535:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The target url has an invalid port.\\\")\\n\\n literal_ip = None\\n try:\\n literal_ip = ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)\\n except ValueError:\\n literal_ip = None\\n\\n if literal_ip is not None:\\n ascii_host = str(literal_ip)\\n addresses = [ascii_host]\\n else:\\n host = hostname.rstrip(\\\".\\\")\\n if not host:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The target url must include a host.\\\")\\n try:\\n ascii_host = host.encode(\\\"idna\\\").decode(\\\"ascii\\\").lower()\\n except (UnicodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\n \\\"The host of the target url is not a valid domain name.\\\"\\n ) from exc\\n if len(ascii_host) > MAX_HOSTNAME_LENGTH:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\\"The host of the target url is too long.\\\")\\n default_port = 443 if scheme == \\\"https\\\" else 80\\n addresses = _resolve(ascii_host, port if port is not None else default_port)\\n\\n for address in addresses:\\n try:\\n resolved = ipaddress.ip_address(address)\\n except ValueError as exc:\\n raise InvalidURLError(\\n \\\"The host of the target url resolved to an unusable address.\\\"\\n ) from exc\\n if
